faq: Is GHK-Cu peptide legal?

For pharmacy compounding, FDA treats GHK-Cu differently by route. On FDA's May 2026 list, GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes is in Category 1, still under evaluation, and FDA plans to consult its advisory committee before the end of February 2027. Injectable GHK-Cu is on FDA's list of substances whose Category 2 nominations were withdrawn, where FDA notes a possible risk of immune reactions and limited human safety data; that list is not an approval. Health Canada named GHK-Cu among unauthorized injectable peptides in April 2026.

faq: What is the best peptide to stimulate HGH?

No source on this page ranks them; what separates them is what FDA has recorded about safety. FDA notes serious adverse events with CJC-1295, including increased heart rate and a systemic vasodilatory reaction, and calls the clinical data limited. For ipamorelin, FDA cites a published study that identified serious adverse events, including death, when ipamorelin was given intravenously to improve gastric motility. Compare the education pages for CJC-1295 with DAC, Ipamorelin and Tesamorelin before choosing a compound for a study.

faq: Why can't you buy BPC 157 anymore?

BPC-157 is still sold here, labeled for research use only. The restrictions are on pharmacy compounding. FDA placed BPC-157 in Category 2, its group for significant safety concerns, and after the nominators withdrew it FDA still lists possible immune reactions, impurity problems and too little safety information to know whether it would harm people. An FDA advisory committee narrowly backed it for compounding in July 2026, but FDA must still accept that nonbinding vote and go through rulemaking.

faq: Where can I buy the Wolverine stack?

The Wolverine Stack is in this category: one vial holding BPC-157 and TB-500, with the amount of each shown on its product page. Blends draw regulatory attention: in August 2026 warning letters, FDA called two other sellers' blends unapproved new drugs, including one described as tesamorelin 10 mg plus ipamorelin 3 mg. For prescription drugs, FDA allows a fixed combination only when each component contributes to the claimed effects and each component's dosage keeps the combination safe and effective for the patients its labeling defines. BPC-157 and TB-500 are also sold as single vials.

faq: Is DSIP good for sleep?

No source behind this page shows that it is. FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee reviewed DSIP, which FDA calls emideltide, on July 24, 2026, for opioid withdrawal, chronic insomnia and narcolepsy. Trade press reported that the committee voted 7 to 6, with 1 abstention, against adding it to the 503A bulks list, the only one of the seven peptides reviewed that month to be turned down. That vote was about pharmacy compounding, not a verdict on the sleep research, which the DSIP education page reviews.

faq: What is the PT-141 injection used for?

PT-141 is another name for bremelanotide. FDA approved bremelanotide on June 21, 2019 as Vyleesi, a prescription drug. Its label covers one use: acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women, meaning low sexual desire that causes marked distress or interpersonal difficulty and is not due to another medical or psychiatric condition, relationship problems, or a medication or drug substance. A prescriber sets the dose. The PT-141 vial sold here is not that product. It is a vial labeled: For research use only. Not for human or veterinary use.

It is an engineered analog of human GLP-1 with two amino acid substitutions and a fatty acid side chain that binds it tightly to albumin, a blood protein. This research vial holds semaglutide as a white, freeze-dried solid (2 mg, 5 mg), labeled for research use only, with no diluent included.
faq: What strengths does the semaglutide research vial come in?

It comes in 2 mg, 5 mg. That figure is the labeled amount of semaglutide in the vial as a dry solid, not a concentration. The concentration depends on how much diluent is added, and the reconstitution calculator does that arithmetic. The price for each strength shows in the selector above.

pages.summary: A pack of 10 insulin syringes with 1 mL barrels, as listed by the supplier. Insulin syringes are graduated in units, not milliliters: U-100 insulin holds 100 units per mL, so one unit on a U-100 syringe is 0.01 mL.
faq: How many mL is 1 unit on an insulin syringe?

On a U-100 insulin syringe, 100 units fill 1 mL, so 1 unit is 0.01 mL. FDA gives the same math: a 5-unit dose drawn with a U-100 (1 mL) syringe is 0.05 mL. A unit is a volume, not an amount of drug; the units converter switches between mL and U-100 units.

pages.summary: This vial is sold as HGH 10 IU, a freeze-dried (lyophilized) powder for laboratory research. HGH (human growth hormone, or somatropin) is a 191-amino-acid protein hormone made by the pituitary gland. Licensed somatropin medicines are prescription biologics in the US. At the WHO conversion of 3.0 IU per mg, 10 IU equals about 3.3 mg of somatropin.
faq: Where does HGH ship from?

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. The selector at the top of this page lists each origin for the 10 IU vial with its own stock status, so you can see which origin will fill your order before checkout. Delivery details are on the shipping page.

pages.summary: Bacteriostatic water is sterile water for injection with benzyl alcohol added as a preservative, so a vial can be entered more than once. Its FDA-approved label limits it to diluting or dissolving injectable drugs. The supplier lists 0.9% benzyl alcohol.
faq: Can I buy bacteriostatic water at CVS?

In the US, the FDA-approved product (Hospira, NDA 018802) has prescription marketing status and its label says 'Rx only', so a pharmacy supplies it as a prescription item. Our sources do not cover any one chain's stock. The vial on this page is listed for laboratory research use under our research use policy.

pages.summary: This vial is sold as HCG 5000 IU, a freeze-dried powder labeled for laboratory research. HCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is a glycoprotein hormone made by the placenta, built from a 92-amino-acid alpha subunit and a 145-amino-acid beta subunit. It acts almost exactly like luteinizing hormone (LH). Licensed hCG medicines are prescription biologics in the US.
faq: Where does HCG ship from?

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. This vial is listed with a USA origin and a Canada origin, and the selector at the top of the page shows the stock status of each. An origin marked out of stock cannot fill the order. Delivery details are on the shipping page.

pages.summary: BPC-157 is a lab-made pentadecapeptide, a 15-amino-acid fragment of body protection compound, a protein found in human gastric juice. The vial holds 5 mg as freeze-dried powder, which FDA describes as white to off-white. Published research is mostly in rats, and FDA found no country where a BPC-157 medicine is approved.

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. Each origin is a separate option in the selector at the top of this page, with its own stock status, so you can pick one before checkout. Delivery details are on the shipping page, and return terms are on the returns page.

pages.summary: Sermorelin is a synthetic peptide that matches the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), with an amidated end. It binds the GHRH receptor and prompts the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. This vial holds 10 mg of sermorelin as a freeze-dried powder for laboratory research. It is not currently FDA-approved: FDA withdrew its approvals for sermorelin (sold as Geref) in 2009.

pages.summary: This research vial holds retatrutide (research code LY3437943) as a freeze-dried powder, sold in 10 mg, 30 mg strengths. Retatrutide is a lab-made peptide of 39 amino acids with a fatty-acid side chain. In cell tests, the one molecule activates three hormone receptors: GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. Lilly calls it a phase 3 investigational molecule, and no regulator has approved it.
faq: Can I buy retatrutide peptide in the USA?

D2C Peptides sells retatrutide as a research vial, labeled for research use only and shipped across the United States. It is not an approved medicine: no regulator has approved it. Lilly, its developer, says it cannot legally be sold or marketed for human use, and that products claiming to be retatrutide offered for sale to consumers are unlawful. The research use policy sets the terms.

pages.summary: Tesamorelin is a lab-made analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH): all 44 amino acids of the human hormone plus a hexenoyl group. It signals the pituitary to release the body's own growth hormone. FDA has approved it as the prescription injections Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR for one use: reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. The research vials here hold freeze-dried powder in 2 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg sizes and are not Egrifta.
faq: Which tesamorelin strengths are listed?

The listed strengths are 2 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, one strength per vial. Each strength shows its own price and stock status in the selector. These are research quantities. The approved products are packaged differently: Egrifta SV as a 2 mg vial with histidine, mannitol, polysorbate 20 and sucrose, and Egrifta WR as an 11.6 mg vial with hydroxypropyl betadex and mannitol.

pages.summary: GHK-Cu is the copper(II) complex of GHK, a tripeptide of glycine, histidine and lysine that occurs naturally in human plasma. Its cosmetic ingredient name is copper tripeptide-1, and FDA stated in 2020 that it is not a component of any FDA-approved human drug. This vial holds 50 mg of the complex, which the supplier describes as a blue freeze-dried solid.
faq: Can I buy GHK-Cu peptide for human use?

No. You can buy GHK-Cu here only as a research vial, and every vial is labeled: For research use only. Not for human or veterinary use. FDA stated in 2020 that GHK-Cu is not a component of any FDA-approved human drug. FDA says compounded injectable GHK-Cu may pose a risk of immune reactions because of aggregation and peptide-related impurities, and that human data are limited.

pages.summary: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme found widely in nature, including in human cells, where it carries electrons in energy metabolism. It is a dinucleotide, not a peptide. Each vial holds 500 mg of NAD+ as a white freeze-dried solid, with no diluent. It is sold for laboratory research and is not FDA-approved.

pages.summary: PT-141 is the development code for bremelanotide, a lab-made cyclic peptide of seven amino acids that activates melanocortin receptors. Each vial holds 10 mg of PT-141 as a white freeze-dried (lyophilized) solid; bacteriostatic water is sold separately. The only FDA-approved bremelanotide product is Vyleesi, a prescription autoinjector. This vial is sold for laboratory research.
faq: Where can I buy PT-141 nasal spray?

No bremelanotide nasal spray is FDA approved: Drugs@FDA lists only a solution for injection under the skin. Nasal PT-141 was tested against placebo in two studies of men reported in 2004. The only approved product, Vyleesi, is a 1.75 mg/0.3 mL injection in a single-dose autoinjector. This store does not sell a spray. It offers PT-141 only as a 10 mg freeze-dried vial for laboratory research.

Research supplies are synthetic copies of it. This vial holds 10 mg of MOTS-c as a freeze-dried (lyophilized) powder, sold for research use only; the listing does not say whether it is the free base or the acetate salt. MOTS-c is not an FDA-approved drug.
faq: Where can I buy MOTS-c peptide?

D2C Peptides lists MOTS-c as a 10 mg vial of freeze-dried powder, sold for research use only under the store's research use policy. Choose a ship-from option in the selector on this page, and see the shipping page for delivery details. MOTS-c is not an FDA-approved drug and is not part of any approved medicine.

pages.summary: TB-500 is a lab-made peptide of seven amino acids (Ac-LKKTETQ) that matches amino acids 17 to 23 of thymosin beta-4, a natural 43-amino-acid protein. It is a research compound and is not part of any FDA-approved drug. Each vial holds 5 mg of TB-500 as a powder for reconstitution in the lab.

It switches on several melanocortin receptors, and in small trials it darkened skin but also caused erections, nausea and yawning. The vial holds 10 mg of white freeze-dried powder. MT2 is not FDA approved for any use.

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. The selector at the top of this page shows the stock status for each shipping origin before you add the vial to your cart. Delivery details are on the shipping page and return terms on the returns page.

pages.summary: SS-31 (elamipretide) is a synthetic tetrapeptide, a chain of four amino acids, that targets the inner membrane of mitochondria, the energy-producing parts of cells. The FDA label calls elamipretide a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder. Each vial holds 20 mg of SS-31 as a white freeze-dried solid, sold for laboratory research only. It is not Forzinity, the FDA-approved elamipretide injection.

pages.summary: These IGF-1 vials hold IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 IGF-I), a lab-made variant of insulin-like growth factor 1, the hormone that manages the effects of growth hormone. It has 83 amino acids to native IGF-1's 70 and binds IGF-binding proteins about 1,000 times more weakly. Each vial holds white freeze-dried powder, in 0.1 mg, 1 mg sizes. Published studies of it are in cells and animals; ClinicalTrials.gov lists no human trial.

The listings are named IGF-1, but the supplier's specification gives the 83-amino-acid LR3 sequence, and the one lot certificate reviewed matched LR3 by mass. Native IGF-1, the 70-amino-acid hormone, is a different molecule.

This vial holds 2 mg of white freeze-dried solid for laboratory research.

Each vial holds 5 mg as a white freeze-dried (lyophilized) solid. DSIP is not a registered drug in any country FDA searched, and FDA found human data only for intravenous use.

pages.summary: Kisspeptin-10 is a 10-amino-acid peptide, the fully active end piece of kisspeptin-54, a hormone made from the human KISS1 gene. It activates the kisspeptin receptor (KISS1R, also called GPR54); studies in rodents and monkeys show it acts directly on the brain's GnRH nerve cells. The vial holds 5 mg of Kisspeptin-10. Human studies have been small (4 to 46 people) and brief: single doses or infusions of up to 22.5 hours. No kisspeptin product is FDA approved.
faq: Where can I get kisspeptin?

Not as a prescription medicine. DailyMed lists no kisspeptin drug label, and FDA's compounding nominations list puts Kisspeptin-10 in Category 2, for substances that raise significant safety risks. Massachusetts General Hospital studies gave it under FDA oversight, one under an investigational new drug number. This page lists it as a 5 mg research vial for laboratory work, not for use in people.

pages.summary: Thymosin Alpha-1 (drug name thymalfasin) is a synthetic peptide of 28 amino acids with an acetylated N-terminus, sold here as one vial of freeze-dried powder for laboratory research. PubChem classes it as an immunologic adjuvant, a substance that stimulates or modulates immune responses. FDA has approved no drug that contains it.
faq: Where can I buy thymosin alpha 1?

This page sells Thymosin Alpha-1 as a freeze-dried vial for laboratory research, with stock and the current price for each shipping origin in the selector. It is not for use in people. It is also not Zadaxin, the brand approved abroad: FDA calls Zadaxin a finished drug product that cannot be used interchangeably with Ta1 as a substance.

pages.summary: This vial is sold as HMG 75 IU, a freeze-dried powder for laboratory research. HMG (menotropins) is a mixture of gonadotropin hormones extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women and then purified. Its follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) activity is measured in international units, and hCG is also present. The licensed US product, Menopur, is a prescription biologic.

pages.summary: KPV is a short peptide of three amino acids, lysine, proline and valine, that matches positions 11 to 13 of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). FDA reports it can be made by solid-phase peptide synthesis and is not a component of any FDA-approved drug. This vial holds 10 mg of a white freeze-dried solid, as the supplier describes it.

This listing is a 5 mg vial of freeze-dried GHRP-6 for laboratory research. It has no approved label (DailyMed lists none), and FDA names it among compounding substances that may present significant safety risks.

GHRP-6 has more than one listed shipping origin, and availability can differ between them, so check the selector at the top of this page for each origin's price and stock before checkout. Russia registers it as a nonprescription anti-anxiety nasal drop, and it is not FDA-approved. Each vial holds 5 mg as a white freeze-dried (lyophilized) solid.
faq: Where can I buy Selank peptide?

This page lists Selank for sale as a 5 mg vial of freeze-dried powder for laboratory research. Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States, and the selector at the top of the page shows stock for each shipping origin before checkout. Selank is not FDA-approved. In Russia it is a different finished product, nasal drops dispensed without a prescription.

It joins a modified 29-amino-acid GRF(1-29) chain to an extra lysine that carries a maleimide group, the drug affinity complex (DAC), built to bind albumin in the blood. The vial holds 2 mg for laboratory research as freeze-dried (lyophilized) powder, the form FDA describes for CJC-1295 DAC. No form of CJC-1295 is part of an FDA-approved drug.

Japan approved it in 2004 solely for a one-time diagnostic test for growth hormone deficiency, and it has no FDA approval. This vial holds 5 mg of GHRP-2 for laboratory research.
faq: Where does GHRP-2 ship from?

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. Each shipping origin for GHRP-2 has its own stock status, so choose one in the selector to see whether it is available and what it costs before checkout. Delivery options are explained on the shipping page.

The vial is listed as 2 mg of gonadorelin acetate. Its clinical uses have included testing pituitary function and pulse therapy by infusion pump in hypothalamic amenorrhea. Both FDA-approved human products are discontinued; the remaining FDA-approved gonadorelin products are cattle drugs.
faq: Where does Gonadorelin ship from?

Gonadorelin ships from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. Stock is tracked separately for each origin, and the Ships from options above mark any origin that is out of stock before checkout. Delivery details are on the shipping page, and return terms are on the returns page.

pages.summary: ARA-290, also called cibinetide, is a lab-made peptide of 11 amino acids modeled on the helix B surface of erythropoietin (EPO). It was designed to keep EPO's tissue-protective signaling without stimulating red blood cell production. This listing is one 10 mg vial of freeze-dried powder, sold for laboratory research. ARA-290 holds orphan drug designations in the US and EU but is not an approved medicine.
faq: Where does ARA-290 ship from?

Orders go out from the USA and Canada and ship across the United States. ARA-290 is listed with two shipping origins, and the selector above shows whether each has the vial in stock before it goes in your cart. Processing, delivery and other shipping details are on the shipping page.

Nearly all published work is cell culture from that group, and no clinical trial is registered. It is not an FDA-approved drug. Each vial holds 20 mg of freeze-dried powder, sold for laboratory research.

The selector at the top of this page lists each shipping origin for the vial with its stock status, so you can check availability before checkout. It is designed to prompt the pituitary to release growth hormone, but FDA found no pharmacology studies of this form, and a 2026 review found no peer-reviewed human studies. Vladimir Khavinson's group in St. Petersburg, Russia, designed it from epithalamin, an extract of cattle pineal glands. Research on it is mostly in cells and animals, on telomeres, melatonin and aging. The vial holds 10 mg of white freeze-dried powder. It is not FDA approved.

The Epithalon price is 30 for one 10 mg vial of freeze-dried powder; the price and stock badge at the top of the page update for each shipping origin. Studies have tested it in nerve cells, rats and Alzheimer's model mice. Human data are limited to a few Russian studies. Each vial holds 20 mg of white freeze-dried powder, sold for laboratory research.

Orders ship from the USA and Canada to addresses across the United States. The options at the top of the page show each shipping origin offered and its stock status before the vial goes in your cart. Delivery details are on the shipping page, and the returns page sets out return terms.

Our tirzepatide price runs from $100 to $280 per research vial (5 mg, 20 mg, 30 mg), and the figure worth comparing is tirzepatide cost per mg: the vial price divided by the milligrams it holds. Cost per mg is only as reliable as what the vial really contains, so read the lot certificate before you compare vendors. Research-labeled tirzepatide is not an FDA-approved drug.
faq: What is tirzepatide in peptide form?

Tirzepatide is a linear chain of 39 amino acids with a C20 fatty diacid joined through a linker to the lysine at position 20. Its FDA label says it binds to and activates the receptors for two hormones, GIP and GLP-1, and that the fatty diacid lets it bind albumin, which prolongs its half-life. Research vials are sold by weight: the strength on the label is the milligrams of peptide the vial is meant to hold.

faq: What is semaglutide peptide?

Semaglutide is a peptide of 31 amino acids. It is an analogue of the human hormone GLP-1 with two amino acid substitutions: Aib at position 8 and Arg at position 34. The lysine at position 26 carries a hydrophilic spacer and a C18 fatty diacid. Research vials are sold by weight: the strength on the label is the milligrams of peptide the vial is meant to hold.

faq: Is retatrutide a peptide?

Yes. Retatrutide is a synthetic peptide of 39 amino acids with a fatty-acid side chain. Lilly's discovery paper describes it as a triple agonist peptide at the glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 receptors. PubChem's systematic name shows a 20-carbon fatty diacid attached through a linker to the lysine at position 17. Research vials are sold by weight: the strength on the label is the milligrams of peptide the vial is meant to hold.

pages.summary: A peptide is a short chain of amino acids, typically 2 to 50, linked by peptide bonds. More than 80 peptide drugs have been approved worldwide, with insulin counted as the first, while unapproved research peptides rest mainly on animal studies and scarce human safety data. These pages explain each compound with cited sources.
faq: What is the difference between a peptide and a protein?

Mostly length. A peptide is usually a chain of 2 to 50 amino acids, a chain of 51 or more is a polypeptide, and proteins are built from one or more polypeptides. FDA's biologics rules use a lower cutoff: a defined chain of more than 40 amino acids counts as a protein. Thymosin beta-4, with 43 amino acids, sits above that line, while TB-500, a 7-amino-acid piece of it, sits well below.

pages.summary: This directory links a profile for every peptide and peptide medicine on the site, 51 in all, grouped below by research area. Approved medicines are described from their FDA labels and research compounds from published studies and FDA reviews, with the evidence level named in each health sentence.
faq: Which compounds in this directory are FDA-approved medicines?

Several are. Semaglutide (in Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy) and tirzepatide (in Mounjaro and Zepbound) are FDA-approved GLP-1 medicines. Somatropin (HGH) products are approved for growth hormone deficiency, tesamorelin as EGRIFTA SV, bremelanotide as Vyleesi and elamipretide (SS-31) as Forzinity. Many others are not: no form of CJC-1295 or ipamorelin is a component of an FDA-approved drug. Each profile's key facts table states the compound's status.

pages.summary: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) is a hormone released by the intestine. It helps lower blood sugar after eating and acts in brain areas that control appetite. GLP-1 drugs mimic it: semaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor, tirzepatide adds the GIP receptor, and retatrutide, still investigational, adds the glucagon receptor as well.
faq: What does GLP-1 stand for?

GLP-1 stands for glucagon-like peptide-1. It is a natural hormone made in the intestine. After a meal it helps bring blood sugar down, and it signals brain areas that regulate appetite and food intake. People also use GLP-1 as shorthand for the medicines that copy the hormone, which FDA calls GLP-1 receptor agonists. Semaglutide and liraglutide are two examples.

pages.summary: Bacteriostatic water, the most searched peptide supply, is sterile water with 0.9% or 1.1% benzyl alcohol added as a preservative, and its FDA-approved label limits it to diluting or dissolving drugs. It is one of the lab supplies, with syringes, needles and swabs, used to mix and measure a freeze-dried vial.
faq: Is bacteriostatic water just sterile water?

No. Sterile water for injection has no preservative and comes only in single-dose containers, so whatever is left after one use is discarded. Bacteriostatic water adds benzyl alcohol, which limits bacterial growth so a multiple-dose vial can be re-entered, generally for up to 28 days after first entry. The same preservative is why it is kept away from newborns and from drugs that need preservative-free water.

pages.summary: Research peptides are lab-made peptides sold with wording such as "for research use only" instead of as approved medicines. That wording echoes FDA labeling rules for lab tests and for drugs shipped for test-tube or animal research, and FDA has found that it does not stop a product from being an unapproved drug when the seller's website shows it is meant for people.
faq: What does "research use only" mean on a peptide?

It is labeling language, not a permission for any use in people. In FDA rules, "For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures." is the label for lab tests still in the research phase, and a new drug shipped only for test-tube or lab animal work must carry a caution that ends "Not for use in humans." Testing an unapproved drug in people is done under an Investigational New Drug application.

pages.summary: A peptide blend is one vial that holds two or more peptides, and sellers also call such products stacks. The four blends sold here contain six different peptides. No published study has tested KLOW or Glow as mixed, no clinical trial has tested CJC-1295 with ipamorelin, and the one controlled study of BPC-157 with TB-500, in rats, found no added benefit over either peptide alone.
faq: What's the difference between KLOW and Glow peptides?

Glow's 60 mg vial holds three peptides: GHK-Cu (50 mg) plus BPC-157 and TB-500 (5 mg each). KLOW holds the same three plus KPV in a 70 mg vial, and the amount of each peptide is not disclosed. Neither blend has been tested in a published study, and FDA found no clinical studies or human exposure data for KPV by any route. No study compares the two.

pages.summary: The peptides with the strongest weight-loss evidence are the GLP-1 medicines, with average losses of about 15% to 25% of body weight in large trials. Semaglutide (Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) are FDA approved for weight reduction, while retatrutide is still investigational. For most other compounds here, the evidence is animal data or human studies that found no weight loss, as with AOD-9604 and HCG. This page maps what published sources report on each and makes no promise.
faq: How long will it take to lose 20 lbs on Ozempic?

The Ozempic label gives no such timeline, and Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes, not weight loss. In a 30-week diabetes trial of Ozempic alone, average weight fell 3.8 kg on 0.5 mg and 4.7 kg on 1 mg, against 1.2 kg on placebo. In a 40-week trial it fell 5.6 kg on 1 mg and 6.4 kg on 2 mg, all short of 20 pounds (about 9 kg). Results vary from person to person, and the prescriber sets the dose.
Can Mounjaro be used for weight loss only?

Not under its US label. Mounjaro is approved to improve blood sugar control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. It is also approved to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. Weight loss is not one of its indications. The same drug, tirzepatide, is approved for weight reduction under the name Zepbound. In Mounjaro's adult diabetes trials, average weight change ranged from -5.4 to -11.3 kg over 40 to 52 weeks. The prescriber decides which product fits and sets the dose.

pages.summary: No peptide on this page has trial evidence that it builds both muscle and strength in healthy people. Even growth hormone itself added about 2 kg of lean mass in trials of fit young adults, partly as body water, without clear strength gains. The growth hormone releasers were mostly tested for hormone levels, not muscle. This page maps what published sources report on each compound and makes no promise.
faq: Can CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin help with muscle growth?

That has not been shown in people. A 2026 review calls controlled evidence for the pair limited, and the human studies of each peptide measured growth hormone, IGF-1 or gut recovery after surgery, not muscle. The combination improved muscle force only in mice with steroid-induced muscle loss. Even growth hormone itself, which these peptides release, added about 2 kg of lean mass in fit young adults without clear strength gains.
Does IGF-1 LR3 increase muscle?

No registered human trial has tested it: a ClinicalTrials.gov search for IGF-1 LR3 and its other names returns no studies. Over 14 days in growing female rats it increased weight gain and nitrogen retention, while muscle protein synthesis rose only slightly. Trials of recombinant human IGF-1, a different form, found no lean mass gain in 16 older women over a year or in 56 athletes over 28 days.

pages.summary: GHK-Cu, a copper peptide used in skin and hair cosmetics, is the compound here most tied to skin care. Most of its human trials are small studies of facial creams, and no controlled trial has tested it as an injection. Neither blend sold for skin, Glow or KLOW, has been studied as a mixture. This page maps what published sources report on each compound searched with skin and hair, and makes no promise.
faq: Is GHK-Cu peptide good for hair growth?

The human evidence is one small study. In a 2026 randomized split-face trial of 18 adults, eyebrows treated with a 2% GHK-Cu serum gained hair count and diameter, while the placebo side showed no significant change. The hair follicle study often quoted for GHK-Cu tested AHK-Cu, a different copper peptide, and a scalp trial used GHK with 5-aminolevulinic acid instead of copper. No trial of injected GHK-Cu for hair was found.
Does the glow peptide work?

No study has tested the Glow blend of GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500: a PubMed search for the blend names with these peptides returns nothing. Its skin case borrows from topical GHK-Cu, where the human data are 12-week cream studies and a 13-patient laser study with no objective benefit. Controlled trials of injected GHK-Cu are absent, and FDA holds one report of skin and gum darkening with a BPC-157 and TB-500 product.

pages.summary: No peptide on this page has been shown in a modern controlled trial to help people fall or stay asleep. The delta sleep peptide (DSIP) rests on small, conflicting insomnia studies that FDA called inconclusive in 2026. The large modern trials concern sleep apnea, a breathing disorder, not insomnia. This page maps what published sources report on each compound searched with sleep, and makes no promise.
faq: Is DSIP good for sleep?

The evidence is mixed and old: human studies date back to 1981, and the two placebo-controlled insomnia studies were published in 1987 and 1992. Small intravenous studies by one research group reported better sleep in chronic insomnia, while those two double-blind studies by other groups found little or no benefit. FDA's 2026 review called the results inconclusive and at best preliminary. Every human study it found gave DSIP by vein, so neither the under-the-skin route proposed for compounding nor the nasal sprays sold online have been tested.
Does Epithalon make you sleepy?

No study has measured drowsiness or sleep after epitalon. Its human studies looked at melatonin markers, clock genes and an eye disease instead. In night-shift women with low melatonin output, 20 days of a sublingual spray raised a urine melatonin metabolite 1.7-fold, with no change on placebo. FDA's 2026 review concluded there is a lack of evidence that it works for insomnia. Whether it causes sleepiness or improves sleep is unknown.

pages.summary: The tanning peptides are lab-made versions of alpha-MSH, the hormone that darkens skin. Melanotan 2 is not FDA approved, and its only tanning data come from a 1996 pilot study in which 2 of 3 men darkened. Melanotan 1 (afamelanotide) is approved only as Scenesse, an implant for adults with phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria. This page maps what published sources report on each and makes no promise.
faq: What is better, melanotan 1 or 2?

Neither is approved for cosmetic tanning, and they differ in structure, receptors and status. Melanotan 1 (afamelanotide) is a linear peptide that binds mainly MC1R, the pigment receptor. It is FDA approved as Scenesse, an implant for adults with phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP). Melanotan 2 is a shorter, ring-shaped peptide that switches on several melanocortin receptors, and its human studies reported nausea and erections. It is not FDA approved.
Does melanotan 2 affect the heart?

Animal studies and case reports suggest it can. In conscious mice, Melanotan 2 raised blood pressure and heart rate in a dose-dependent way. In rats, a 10-day infusion into the brain raised heart rate by about 27 beats per minute. A man who injected Melanotan 2 bought online to darken his skin had a heart rate of up to 146 beats per minute, followed by muscle breakdown and kidney problems.

pages.summary: Most healing evidence for these peptides comes from rats, not people: of 36 BPC-157 studies in one review, 35 were preclinical. Human data are thin: the three BPC-157 studies in people had 30 participants and no control group. One of the few controlled positive results is a 1994 trial of a copper peptide (GHK-Cu) gel on diabetic foot ulcers. This page maps what published sources report on each peptide searched with healing and recovery, and makes no promise.
faq: What are the key differences between TB500 and BPC-157?

They are different molecules. BPC-157 is a 15-amino-acid peptide based on a protein found in human gastric juice, while TB-500 is a short fragment of thymosin beta-4 (LKKTETQ). BPC-157 has many rat studies and three small human studies. TB-500 has a few animal and cell studies. FDA's May 2026 review found no article in which it was given to people, and a later 2026 report describes 3 dental patients who received it with other drugs. WADA bans both at all times, BPC-157 as a non-approved substance and TB-500 as a growth factor.
Is thymosin alpha 1 the same as TB500?

No. Thymosin alpha-1 is a 28-amino-acid immune peptide isolated from calf thymus in 1977, while TB-500 is a seven-amino-acid fragment of a different protein, thymosin beta-4. Thymosin alpha-1 was studied for infections, cancers and vaccine response, and FDA found a lack of evidence for the 12 uses it reviewed. TB-500 is promoted for tissue repair, but FDA found no article in which it was given to people.

pages.summary: No compound on this page has consistent evidence of better memory or focus in people: in the largest trials, oral semaglutide did not slow early Alzheimer's disease in 3,808 people, and tesamorelin's better executive function in 152 older adults was not repeated in two later, smaller trials. This page maps the peptides people look up for focus, memory and brain health and what published sources report on each one; it makes no promise. Most findings come from cell studies, rodents or small human studies with weak controls.
faq: Is Semax good for ADHD?

The evidence is thin. In 2026 a Russian expert council rated Semax as an add-on drug for children and adolescents with ADHD, with a limited evidence base. A 2007 paper that proposed Semax for ADHD put forward a hypothesis; it was not a trial. No Semax study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, and Semax is not FDA approved.
Is Selank a nootropic?

Russia registers Selank as nonprescription nasal drops for anxiety, classed with other anti-anxiety drugs. Its Russian label also claims better memory and attention. Support for that comes mostly from rats, where Selank improved memory retention. In people, a 60-patient Russian trial that compared Selank with the drug phenazepam reported pronounced anti-anxiety effects and mild nootropic effects. It is not FDA approved.

pages.summary: Evidence that any compound here raises testosterone comes only from short studies or narrow groups: kisspeptin-10 during IV infusions of up to 22.5 hours in a few men, pulsed gonadorelin in men with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and hCG, which is FDA-approved for selected men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Where growth hormone peptides were studied, LH, the hormone that drives the testes, did not change. This page maps the compounds people search with testosterone and what published sources report on each; it makes no promise.
faq: Does kisspeptin raise testosterone levels?

Briefly, in small studies. Intravenous kisspeptin-10 infusions of 11 to 22.5 hours raised testosterone in 4 healthy men and in 5 men with type 2 diabetes and low testosterone, and single IV doses gave small rises; none of these studies lasted much longer than a day. A 75-minute infusion of the longer kisspeptin-54 did not change it in 32 men with low sexual desire. In phase 1 studies of healthy men, long-acting kisspeptin analogs given continuously did the opposite, pushing testosterone below the castration level within 7 to 8 days.
Does IGF-1 LR3 increase testosterone?

There is no evidence either way. No study reviewed here measured testosterone after IGF-1 LR3, in people or in animals; published LR3 research looked at growth, nitrogen balance and protein turnover in cells and rats. A ClinicalTrials.gov search in October 2026 found no registered human LR3 trial. Mecasermin (Increlex), an FDA-approved form of IGF-1, is indicated for growth failure in children 2 years and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency.

pages.summary: Most results on this page come from small, short studies; the largest body of evidence is for prescription hormone therapy in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, which produced sperm in 75% of men who had none across 44 studies. Studies of peptides for erections and libido are mostly small, and none of those peptides is approved for erectile dysfunction. This page maps what people search as peptides for men and what published sources report on each; it makes no promise, and testosterone has its own page.
faq: What are the benefits of sermorelin for men?

The studies are small and short. In 10 older men, two weeks at the higher of two doses raised growth hormone and IGF-1 to the levels of young men. In an uncontrolled 6-week study of 11 men aged 64 to 76, 2 of 6 strength measures improved, and body composition did not change. These trials measured hormones, strength and body composition, not long-term health. The approved sermorelin product, Geref, was discontinued, and FDA withdrew its approval in 2009.
What are the potential side effects of HGH in men?

In a 26-week randomized trial of older men, 41% of those given growth hormone had joint pain, and carpal tunnel symptoms affected 32% of men given growth hormone plus testosterone. Diabetes or glucose intolerance was also more common with growth hormone (18 against 7 men). In a review of healthy older adults, breast enlargement (gynecomastia) was more common with growth hormone. Somatropin is a prescription drug, and the prescriber sets the dose.

pages.summary: Only the GLP-1 drugs on this page have large trials showing lower blood sugar: in adults with type 2 diabetes, the approved diabetes brands Ozempic, Rybelsus and Mounjaro lowered HbA1c by about 1.2 to 2.4 points. The other peptides here have small, early or animal data, and growth hormone peptides can work against blood sugar control. This page maps what people search with blood sugar and what published sources report on each; it makes no promise.
faq: Which GLP-1 medicines are approved for type 2 diabetes?

FDA-approved GLP-1 medicines for type 2 diabetes include Ozempic injection and tablets and Rybelsus (semaglutide), Mounjaro (tirzepatide), Victoza (liraglutide), Trulicity (dulaglutide), and Byetta and Bydureon BCise (exenatide). Wegovy and Zepbound, which contain semaglutide and tirzepatide, are approved for weight and related uses, not to treat diabetes. In each case the prescriber sets the dose.
Is retatrutide approved for diabetes?

No. As of October 2026, retatrutide is not approved by FDA or any other regulator. FDA says it is not a component of any approved drug, has not been found safe and effective for any condition, and cannot be used in compounding. In a 40-week phase 3 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c fell 1.69 to 1.94 percentage points against 0.81 on placebo. It has no established role in type 1 diabetes; one case report describes impending diabetic ketoacidosis in a person with type 1 diabetes who used online-sourced retatrutide.

pages.summary: Bremelanotide (Vyleesi) is FDA-approved for low sexual desire in premenopausal women, with small average benefits in its trials, and hCG and HMG are approved fertility drugs; most research peptides on this page have little or no data in women. This page maps what people search with women's health and what published sources report on each, including pregnancy and birth control advice on medicine labels; it makes no promise.
faq: Which peptide medicine is approved for low sexual desire in women?

Bremelanotide, sold as Vyleesi. FDA approved it only for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD): low desire that developed after a time of normal desire, occurs regardless of situation or partner, causes marked distress, and is not explained by another condition, relationship problems or a medicine. It is not approved for postmenopausal women or to enhance sexual performance. It is a prescription medicine, and the prescriber sets the dose. Kisspeptin and Melanotan 2 are not FDA approved for any use.
Is kisspeptin used in IVF?

Only in research so far, and with kisspeptin-54 rather than kisspeptin-10. In a 2015 phase 2 trial, a single kisspeptin-54 injection matured eggs in 95% of 60 women at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation, and none developed moderate or severe OHSS. The researchers say large randomized comparisons with standard triggers are still needed. Kisspeptin-10 itself did not raise reproductive hormones in women in the follicular phase of the cycle, only in the preovulatory phase.

pages.summary: Most GLP-1 brand names come down to a few molecules: Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy all contain semaglutide, and Mounjaro and Zepbound both contain tirzepatide, so brands that share a molecule differ in approved uses, forms and doses. These pages set the medicines side by side, one pair per page, and two head-to-head trials compare tirzepatide with semaglutide directly.
faq: Are Victoza and Saxenda the same?

They contain the same active ingredient, liraglutide, and both are daily injections from Novo Nordisk, but their labels differ. Victoza, at up to 1.8 mg a day, is approved for type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older, and to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease. Saxenda, at 3 mg a day, is approved for long-term weight reduction in adults and children 12 and older who weigh more than 60 kg and have obesity, and in adults with overweight and at least one weight-related condition.

pages.subject: tirzepatide
pages.summary: Tirzepatide is a modified peptide, built on the sequence of the gut hormone GIP, that activates the receptors for two gut hormones, GIP and GLP-1, and has a half-life of about 5 days. It is the active ingredient in two prescription medicines: Mounjaro, approved in 2022 for type 2 diabetes, and Zepbound, approved in 2023 for chronic weight management.
faq: Is there still a shortage of tirzepatide?

No. Tirzepatide injection had been in shortage since 2022. FDA declared the shortage resolved on October 2, 2024, re-evaluated that decision, and confirmed it on December 19, 2024. As of FDA's April 1, 2026 update, tirzepatide is not on the drug shortage list. FDA's temporary leniency for compounders, which depended on the shortage listing, ended in March 2025.
Is tirzepatide the same as Ozempic?

No. Ozempic's active ingredient is semaglutide, which the authors of a head-to-head trial describe as a selective GLP-1 receptor agonist. Tirzepatide is a different molecule that activates both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In that 40-week trial of 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes, every tirzepatide dose lowered HbA1c more than semaglutide 1 mg. More detail: Ozempic vs Tirzepatide.
facts: Dual GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist; MedlinePlus groups it with the incretin mimetics

pages.subject: zepbound
pages.summary: Zepbound is Eli Lilly's brand of tirzepatide, a once-weekly prescription injection that activates GIP and GLP-1 receptors. FDA approved it in November 2023 for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition. In December 2024 it was approved for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.
faq: Is Zepbound the same as Mounjaro?

They contain the same medicine: both are tirzepatide from Eli Lilly, made in the same six dose strengths. Mounjaro is approved for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes, in adults and children 10 and older. It is also approved to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. Zepbound is approved for weight reduction and obstructive sleep apnea, and its label advises against combining it with other tirzepatide products or any GLP-1 receptor agonist.
Do I need a prescription for Zepbound?

Yes. Drugs@FDA lists Zepbound's marketing status as prescription, under Eli Lilly's application NDA 217806. Lilly says the prescription can be filled through LillyDirect or at a retail pharmacy. The weight use covers adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition. The sleep apnea use covers adults with obesity and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea.

pages.subject: mounjaro
pages.summary: Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's brand of tirzepatide, a once-weekly injection that activates the GIP and GLP-1 hormone receptors. FDA approved it in May 2022 for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes, now in adults and children 10 and older. Since August 2026 it is also approved to lower major heart event risk in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes.
faq: Is Zepbound the same as Mounjaro?

Both contain tirzepatide made by Eli Lilly, but each has its own FDA approval. Mounjaro is approved for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes and for lowering major cardiovascular event risk in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. Zepbound is approved to reduce excess body weight and keep it off in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, and to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. The Zepbound label advises against using it with any other tirzepatide product.
Is Mounjaro the same as Ozempic?

No. Ozempic's active ingredient is semaglutide, which acts on the GLP-1 receptor only, while the tirzepatide in Mounjaro activates both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors. Both are once-weekly injections approved for adults with type 2 diabetes. In SURPASS-2, a 40-week trial of 1,879 adults already taking metformin, Mounjaro 5 to 15 mg lowered HbA1c by 2.0 to 2.3 points, against 1.9 points with semaglutide 1 mg.

pages.subject: wegovy
pages.summary: Wegovy is Novo Nordisk's prescription brand of semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, made as a weekly injection and, since December 2025, daily tablets (Wegovy pills). With diet and exercise, it is approved for long-term weight reduction and to lower heart attack and stroke risk in adults with heart disease and excess weight. The injection also treats MASH, a liver disease.
faq: What is the active ingredient in Wegovy?

Semaglutide. Wegovy injection and Wegovy tablets both contain it. Semaglutide is an analog of the hormone GLP-1, with 94% sequence homology to the human hormone and a half-life of about 1 week. Ozempic and Rybelsus contain the same ingredient and are approved for type 2 diabetes. The Wegovy label does not recommend using it with other semaglutide products or any other GLP-1 receptor agonist.
What is Wegovy used for?

The label lists three uses, each with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity. The first is lowering the risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke in adults with heart disease and obesity or overweight. The second is long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, and in children 12 and older with obesity (injection only). The third, for the injection only, is noncirrhotic MASH with F2 to F3 liver fibrosis in adults, under an accelerated approval.

pages.subject: semaglutide
pages.summary: Semaglutide is a lab-made peptide that mimics the hormone GLP-1, sharing 94% of its sequence, with an elimination half-life of about one week. It is the active ingredient in the prescription medicines Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus, FDA approved for type 2 diabetes, weight management and heart, kidney and liver uses.
faq: What is a brand name for semaglutide?

In the US, semaglutide is sold as Ozempic (weekly injection or daily tablets) and Rybelsus (daily tablets), both for type 2 diabetes. Wegovy, a weekly injection (including Wegovy HD 7.2 mg) or daily tablets, is the brand for weight management and heart risk reduction, and the injection also covers the liver disease MASH. In the EU, a semaglutide injection for MASH is authorised as Kayshild. All are Novo Nordisk products.
Is semaglutide a GLP-1 inhibitor?

No. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist: it binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor, the same target as the body's own GLP-1, rather than blocking it. FDA's pharmacologic class for semaglutide is GLP-1 receptor agonist. What it resists is breakdown: the Aib substitution at position 8 protects it from the enzyme DPP-4, one reason its half-life is about a week.
facts: GLP-1 receptor agonist; a peptide of 31 amino acids

pages.subject: bpc157
pages.summary: BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide of 15 amino acids, described as a partial sequence of a protein isolated from human gastric juice. First reported in 1993, it has been studied mostly in rats. Human studies are few, small and short, and no BPC-157 medicine is approved in any country.
faq: What are the key differences between TB500 and BPC-157?

BPC-157 has 15 amino acids and is described as part of a gastric juice protein. TB-500 is LKKTETQ, a seven-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4, and FDA has found no human exposure data for it. WADA bans both at all times, BPC-157 under class S0 and TB-500 under S2. In July 2026, FDA's compounding advisory committee reviewed BPC-157 for ulcerative colitis and TB-500 for wound healing.
What does the peptide BPC-157 do?

In people, no effect has been established: USADA notes that no human clinical trial shows BPC-157 works for any diagnosis or treatment. In rats, it has been reported to improve healing of cut tendons, ligaments and muscle. Cell and rat studies link it to blood-vessel growth signals and to tendon-cell migration. FDA says its molecular targets are still unidentified.
facts: Synthetic peptide of 15 amino acids (a pentadecapeptide)

pages.subject: ghk-cu
pages.summary: GHK-Cu is GHK, a three-amino-acid peptide (glycine, histidine, lysine) found in human plasma, bound to a copper ion. Skin and hair cosmetics use it under the name copper tripeptide-1. It is not an FDA-approved drug. Nearly all human data come from products applied to the skin, and FDA calls human data on injectable GHK-Cu limited.
faq: Which brand is the best for GHK-Cu peptide?

No GHK-Cu product has passed FDA review as a drug, so no brand can point to an approval for use in people. For research vials, compare the test documents instead. The certificate posted by this store's supplier for lot 2025-02-13 reports 99.90% purity by HPLC-UV-MS, with no sterility, endotoxin or content-per-vial results. Lab documents for products sold here are on the lab results page.
What are the benefits of GHK-Cu peptide injections?

No benefit of injected GHK-Cu has been shown in people: the sources reviewed hold no published human trial of it, and a ClinicalTrials.gov search for GHK in October 2026 found none registered. A 2026 orthopaedic review found no clinical data supporting it for musculoskeletal conditions. The injection results come from rodents: less lung injury and lung scarring in mice, less smoke-related muscle loss in mice, and knee-graft healing in rats that faded once treatment stopped.
facts: Metallopeptide: the copper(II) complex of the tripeptide GHK (Gly-His-Lys)

pages.subject: sermorelin
pages.summary: Sermorelin is a lab-made peptide that copies the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). It prompts the pituitary gland to release the body's own growth hormone. FDA approved it as Geref, a test of pituitary growth hormone release and a treatment for growth hormone deficiency in children, but withdrew both approvals in 2009.
faq: What will sermorelin do for my body?

Sermorelin binds GHRH receptors and prompts the pituitary to release growth hormone (GH). Measured effects vary by study. In 10 older men, two weeks on the higher of two tested doses raised GH and IGF-1 to young-adult levels. In a trial of 110 GH-deficient children, it sped up growth. Yet a 6-week study in 11 older men found no change in weight or in DEXA fat and muscle. These are group results from small studies, not predictions for any one person.
Is sermorelin real HGH?

No. Sermorelin is a 29-amino-acid piece of growth hormone-releasing hormone, the signal that leads the pituitary to make and release growth hormone. HGH drugs such as somatropin are growth hormone analogs that work by replacing the hormone itself. Sermorelin works through the pituitary instead, and FDA once approved it as a test of the pituitary's ability to secrete growth hormone.
facts: Synthetic growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog: the 1-29 fragment of human GHRH with an amidated end

pages.subject: pt-141
pages.summary: PT-141 is the development code for bremelanotide, a synthetic ring-shaped peptide of seven amino acids that activates melanocortin receptors. FDA approved it in 2019 as Vyleesi, a prescription autoinjector for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD). It is not approved for men, and research-labeled vials have no approved application.
faq: What is the PT-141 injection used for?

PT-141 is bremelanotide. FDA approved it in 2019, as Vyleesi, for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder: low desire that causes marked distress or interpersonal difficulty and is not explained by another condition, relationship problems or a medicine. The approved form is a 1.75 mg injection under the skin, used as needed. The label excludes men, postmenopausal women and use to enhance sexual performance.
What does PT-141 do for your body?

It activates melanocortin receptors, most potently MC1R and then MC4R. A 2022 review proposes that its effect on desire runs through MC4 receptors in the hypothalamus that raise dopamine release, a model based mainly on animal studies. The label says the exact mechanism in women with HSDD is unknown. Each dose also briefly raises blood pressure and slows heart rate, and repeated use can darken patches of skin.
facts: Synthetic cyclic heptapeptide; melanocortin receptor agonist and alpha-MSH analog

pages.subject: nad
pages.summary: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme in human cells that carries electrons in energy metabolism and is needed by enzymes such as sirtuins and PARPs. It is not a peptide. NAD+ injections are not FDA-approved, and human data on the effects of IV NAD+ remain limited.
faq: Is NAD like Ozempic?

No. Ozempic (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved GLP-1 receptor agonist used with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. NAD+ is a coenzyme, not a GLP-1 drug, and has no FDA approval. Oral NAD+ precursor trials did not show weight loss: ten weeks of NMN left body weight and fat unchanged in 25 women with prediabetes, and twelve weeks of NR had no effect on body composition in 40 obese men. More on the brand: What is Ozempic?
Can you get NAD shots?

Not as an approved product in the US. NAD is in FDA's 503A Category 1. FDA does not intend to act against licensed pharmacies or physicians compounding with Category 1 substances when its conditions are met. Compounding under section 503A needs a valid patient-specific prescription, and compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Even so, the authors of a 2026 clinic study note that IV NAD+ has become widely available in commercial clinics.
facts: Coenzyme; a dinucleotide of a nicotinamide nucleotide and an adenine nucleotide, not a peptide

pages.subject: mots-c
pages.summary: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide coded by a short stretch of mitochondrial DNA, in the 12S rRNA gene. Scientists first described it in 2015 and have studied it mostly in mice, rats and cells for effects on metabolism and insulin sensitivity. It is not an FDA-approved drug, and FDA found no clinical studies of it in people.
faq: What is a MOTS-c shot?

It is an injection of synthetic MOTS-c, a lab-made copy of the natural peptide. FDA found injectable MOTS-c marketed online for uses such as mitochondrial energy, liver fat metabolism, metabolic balance and glucose control. Its 2026 review also found no human studies of MOTS-c by any route, and FDA is concerned that injected MOTS-c could trigger immune reactions because of aggregates and impurities. No FDA-approved drug contains it.
What is MOTS-c peptide used for?

Research on MOTS-c has focused mostly on metabolism. FDA's 2026 review lists the uses it was nominated for: insulin resistance, obesity, osteoporosis, vascular calcification, muscle and fat metabolism, and longevity. The studies behind those uses were done in cells and rodents, not people. MOTS-c has no approved therapeutic use, is not part of any FDA-approved drug, and FDA found no clinical studies of it in people.

pages.subject: ozempic
pages.summary: Ozempic is Novo Nordisk's brand of semaglutide, a prescription GLP-1 receptor agonist. Its weekly injection was approved in 2017 for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes, later adding heart and kidney risk uses. The Ozempic name has covered a daily pill since January 2026. Ozempic is not approved for weight loss.
faq: Is Ozempic a peptide shot?

Yes. Its active ingredient, semaglutide, is a modified version of the human hormone GLP-1 that keeps 94% of the same amino acid sequence. In the approved product the peptide chain is made by yeast fermentation and joined to a fatty acid chain, which lets one injection under the skin last about a week. The same molecule is in Wegovy, a weekly injection at higher doses for weight reduction and heart risk, and in Rybelsus, a daily tablet.
Are peptides the same as Ozempic?

No. Ozempic is one FDA-approved medicine, and its active ingredient, semaglutide, is one specific modified peptide made under FDA oversight. A product is not Ozempic because it contains a peptide, or even semaglutide. FDA says compounded semaglutide is not FDA approved, and that semaglutide sold to consumers as 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption' is an unapproved drug of unknown quality. Ozempic itself is dispensed only on prescription.

pages.subject: rybelsus
pages.summary: Rybelsus is Novo Nordisk's once-daily tablet of semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist. It is a prescription medicine for adults with type 2 diabetes. The label covers blood sugar control with diet and exercise and, since October 2025, lowering the risk of cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke in adults at high risk.
faq: Is Rybelsus a prescription drug?

Yes. Rybelsus is available in the US only with a prescription, and as of October 2026 Drugs@FDA lists all three strengths (3 mg, 7 mg and 14 mg) with the marketing status Prescription. Its labeled uses are for adults with type 2 diabetes. Whether it suits a patient, and at which dose, is the prescriber's decision.
What are the key differences between Ozempic and Rybelsus?

Both contain semaglutide and come from Novo Nordisk, but they are different products. Rybelsus is a tablet taken once a day by mouth. The Ozempic injection is a once-weekly shot from a prefilled pen, at doses from 0.25 mg up to a maximum of 2 mg. Its label also covers kidney risk reduction in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, a use the Rybelsus label does not include. Since January 2026, the Ozempic name also covers a daily tablet that shares the Rybelsus label. See Ozempic vs Rybelsus.
facts: GLP-1 receptor agonist; the active ingredient is semaglutide

pages.subject: tb-500
pages.summary: TB-500 (also written TB500) is a lab-made peptide of seven amino acids, Ac-LKKTETQ. It copies positions 17 to 23 of thymosin beta-4, a natural 43-amino-acid protein. It is not part of any FDA-approved drug. FDA's May 2026 review found no published study in which it was given to people.
faq: What is the TB500 peptide used for?

TB-500 has no approved medical use. A veterinary preparation appeared in 2011, marketed to boost performance in horse and greyhound sports. Today it is marketed online for tissue repair, healing of tendons, muscles and ligaments, reducing inflammation and other uses. FDA found no human studies behind any of these uses and concluded there is a lack of evidence to evaluate it for wound healing.
Is thymosin beta-4 (TB4) the same as TB500?

No. Thymosin beta-4 is a natural protein of 43 amino acids with a molar mass of about 4963 g/mol. TB-500 is a lab-made, acetylated piece of it: 7 amino acids and 889.0 g/mol. FDA notes that several websites use the names interchangeably, but says they are not the same substance. The small human trials of IV infusions, eye drops and a topical form tested thymosin beta-4, not TB-500.
facts: Synthetic peptide: an N-acetylated heptapeptide (7 amino acids)

pages.subject: wolverine-stack
pages.summary: The Wolverine stack is a nickname for one vial holding two lab-made peptides, neither FDA-approved: BPC-157, 15 amino acids based on a gastric juice protein, and TB-500, an acetylated 7-amino-acid piece of thymosin beta-4. The pair has been tested in one rat study and in 3 patients without a control group; 4 more got BPC-157 with thymosin beta-4.
faq: What is better, BPC or TB500?

No study in people has compared them. In the closest test, a 2026 study of 32 rats with repaired Achilles tendons, TB-500 alone was the only treatment that significantly raised tendon strength. BPC-157 alone improved tissue scores only numerically, and giving both added nothing over either one. A 2021 knee-pain chart review, with 12 patients on BPC-157 and 4 on BPC-157 plus thymosin beta-4, is too small and uncontrolled to rank them.
Why is it called the Wolverine stack?

The name comes from marketing, not from a study. FDA's 2026 BPC-157 review quotes a clinic website saying the peptide has been called a wolverine compound for its claimed healing properties. FDA's TB-500 review cites a web page about a BPC157 and TB500 wolverine protocol. The healing claims behind the nickname are not established in people: a 2026 systematic review rated the human evidence for BPC-157 as very low certainty.
facts: Blend of two synthetic peptides: BPC-157 (15 amino acids) and TB-500 (an acetylated 7-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4)

pages.subject: melanotan
pages.summary: Melanotan 2 (MT2) is a lab-made, ring-shaped peptide of 7 amino acids modeled on the hormone alpha-MSH. Its few controlled human studies, small University of Arizona trials from 1996 to 2000, found darker skin and erections, with frequent nausea and yawning. It is not an approved medicine in the US or UK.
faq: Does melanotan 2 affect the heart?

Animal data and a case report suggest it can. In conscious mice, MT2 raised blood pressure and heart rate in a dose-dependent way, heart rate more than pressure. A man who injected 6 mg of MT2 bought online had a heart rate that peaked at 146 beats per minute and blood pressure of 151/85, with sweating and tremor. FDA lists sympathomimetic toxidrome among serious events in MT2 case reports. The related approved drug bremelanotide is contraindicated in uncontrolled high blood pressure or known cardiovascular disease. We found no human study of MT2's long-term heart effects.
Can Melanotan 2 make your eyes lighter?

We found no published study or case report showing MT2 changing eye color in either direction. Documented pigment effects include darker skin, new or darker moles, dark nail bands and gum pigmentation. In 2024 FDA quoted an eye-drop seller's website claim that melanotan raises melanin in the eyes, and found that seller's eye-lightening drops to be unapproved new drugs.
facts: Synthetic cyclic heptapeptide (7 amino acids); non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist

pages.subject: cjc-1295-with-dac
pages.summary: CJC-1295 with DAC is a lab-made analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) with an added drug affinity complex (DAC) built to bind albumin in the blood. In small studies of healthy adults, one injection raised growth hormone and IGF-1 for about one to two weeks. It is not approved in the US or the 12 other countries FDA checked.
faq: Is CJC-1295 FDA approved?

No. FDA's 2024 review found that no form of CJC-1295 is a component of an FDA-approved drug, and none has a USP or National Formulary monograph. The review also found no approved CJC-1295 product in any of the 12 other countries it checked, including Canada, Japan and the United Kingdom, and none authorized by the European Medicines Agency.
Is CJC-1295 legal in the US?

CJC-1295 is not an approved drug, and in December 2024 FDA's compounding advisory committee voted 0 to 13 against placing CJC-1295 DAC free base on the list pharmacies may compound from. In an August 2026 warning letter to another peptide seller, FDA said that 'for research use only' and 'not for human or animal consumption' labels did not change its finding that the products were drugs intended for human use.
facts: Synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), a growth hormone secretagogue

pages.subject: klow-peptide
pages.summary: KLOW is a research blend of four peptides, BPC-157, TB-500, KPV and GHK-Cu, freeze-dried together in one vial. The amount of each peptide is not disclosed. No published study has tested the mix in animals or people, and FDA says BPC-157, TB-500 and KPV are not components of any FDA-approved drug.
faq: What does the KLOW peptide do?

No study has tested what KLOW does, in animals or in people. Its four parts have been studied one or two at a time, mostly in animals: BPC-157 and TB-500 on tendon healing in rats, and KPV on gut inflammation in mice. In a 2026 rat study that combined BPC-157 and TB-500 after tendon repair, the pair did no better than either peptide alone. Each finding and its evidence level is on KLOW Peptide Blend benefits and uses.
What is the difference between GLOW and KLOW?

Both are research blends sold as one freeze-dried vial. GLOW combines GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500 and states the amount of each. KLOW holds the same three plus KPV, a three-amino-acid fragment of the hormone alpha-MSH, and states only the total. No published study has tested the KLOW combination, and FDA found no clinical studies or human exposure data for KPV. The other blend is profiled at What is Glow Peptide Stack?.
facts: Peptide blend: four research peptides freeze-dried together in one vial, not a single compound

pages.subject: hgh
pages.summary: HGH (human growth hormone), called somatropin as a drug, is a protein of 191 amino acids that the pituitary gland releases in pulses. It drives growth in children and shapes body composition in adults, partly through IGF-1. In the US it is a prescription drug for growth hormone deficiency and a few other conditions, not for anti-aging.
faq: Is sermorelin real HGH?

No. Sermorelin is a synthetic 29-amino-acid analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), the shortest synthetic peptide with the full biological activity of GHRH. It prompts the anterior pituitary to secrete its own growth hormone, while HGH (somatropin) is the 191-amino-acid hormone itself. In the studies reviewed in 1999, transient facial flushing and injection-site pain were the most commonly reported side effects. More: What is Sermorelin?
Which is better, sermorelin or HGH?

These sources do not settle it. A 1999 review noted that sermorelin at its recommended dosage had not been compared directly with somatropin. In children with growth hormone deficiency, though, sermorelin given as a continuous infusion or in 3 divided doses raised growth rate less than once-daily somatropin at 30 micrograms per kg. Somatropin holds FDA approvals for several growth and deficiency conditions. WADA bans both at all times, growth hormone under S2.2.3 and GHRH analogues under S2.2.4.
facts: Protein hormone of 191 amino acids that activates the growth hormone receptor; drug versions are recombinant somatropin

pages.subject: kpv
pages.summary: KPV is a tripeptide (lysine, proline, valine) that matches the last three amino acids of alpha-MSH, a natural hormone. In cell and animal studies, most often mouse colitis models, it reduced inflammation without alpha-MSH's skin-darkening effect. It is not an approved drug, and FDA's 2026 review found no studies in people.
faq: What is the peptide KPV good for?

In research, KPV has been studied mainly for gut inflammation in mouse colitis models, with smaller lines of work on wounds, skin cells, brain injury and microbes in cells and animals. None of these uses has been tested in people. FDA concluded in 2026 that there is a lack of evidence to evaluate how well KPV works for wound healing or inflammatory conditions. Each area and its evidence level is set out in KPV benefits and uses.
Who shouldn't take KPV peptide?

No group of people is known to be able to use KPV safely, because FDA found no study of it in people. FDA also found no animal toxicity, reproductive or cancer studies, so the risks for anyone, pregnant women included, are unknown. Health Canada tells consumers not to use unauthorized injectable peptides such as KPV. Athletes also face anti-doping rules on unapproved peptides.
facts: Tripeptide (Lys-Pro-Val) matching positions 11 to 13 of alpha-MSH, a melanocortin hormone

pages.subject: glow-peptide
pages.summary: Glow peptide is a blend of three research peptides, not a single compound: the vial sold here holds 50 mg of GHK-Cu, a copper-bound tripeptide, plus 5 mg each of BPC-157 and TB-500. No published study has tested the blend, FDA found no study of TB-500 in people, and none of the ingredients is an approved drug.
faq: Does the glow peptide work?

No published study has tested the Glow blend, in people or in animals, so there is no direct evidence that it works. Research covers the ingredients one at a time. It includes small skin studies of topical GHK-Cu and three small human studies of BPC-157 rated very low certainty. FDA found no human studies of TB-500. A 2026 systematic review called the human GHK-Cu literature thin and fragmented.
What is the best glow peptide?

No Glow product can be called best on evidence, because no Glow blend has been studied or compared. What can be compared is identity. FDA has found multiple salts and derivatives, including different active molecules, sold under the TB-500 name. So for any brand, check whether the lot certificate confirms the identity of each of the three ingredients, not only overall purity.
facts: Peptide blend: three research peptides freeze-dried in one vial, not a single compound

pages.subject: cjc-1295-ipamorelin
pages.summary: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pairs two synthetic peptides designed to make the pituitary release growth hormone by separate routes: CJC-1295 without DAC is a modified form of the hormone GHRH, and ipamorelin mimics ghrelin at its receptor. Neither is an approved medicine, and as of October 2026 no clinical trial has tested the two together.
faq: What is the CJC-1295 ipamorelin peptide?

It is a two-peptide research blend rather than a single molecule. CJC-1295 without DAC, also sold as Mod GRF 1-29, copies the active front section of GHRH with four amino acid swaps, and ipamorelin is a five-amino-acid peptide that activates the ghrelin receptor. The vial sold here holds 10 mg (5 mg + 5 mg). Neither peptide is approved as a medicine, and no trial has tested the pair.
How do I reconstitute CJC-1295/Ipamorelin 5mg/5mg vials?

No official method exists, because the blend has no approved label and no USP monograph. In the lab, the freeze-dried powder is dissolved in a sterile diluent with aseptic technique, and each peptide's concentration is 5 mg divided by the volume of diluent added. FDA reports that CJC-1295 free base is only slightly soluble in water, and compounded versions have been recalled over sterility. Lab steps are in the reconstitution guide.
facts: Two-peptide blend: a GHRH analog (CJC-1295 without DAC) plus a ghrelin-receptor agonist (ipamorelin)

pages.subject: ss-31
pages.summary: SS-31 is the research name for elamipretide, a lab-made peptide of four amino acids that binds cardiolipin, a lipid in the inner membrane of mitochondria. In September 2025, FDA granted accelerated approval to an elamipretide injection, Forzinity, for Barth syndrome in patients weighing at least 30 kg. Research-grade SS-31 has no FDA approval.
faq: Is SS-31 FDA approved?

Only as one prescription product. On September 19, 2025, FDA granted accelerated approval to Forzinity, an elamipretide (SS-31) injection. It is approved to improve muscle strength in Barth syndrome patients weighing at least 30 kg. Research-grade SS-31 vials are not approved: in August 2026, FDA warning letters to four online sellers called their SS-31 products unapproved new drugs.
What's another name for SS-31 peptide?

Its drug name is elamipretide. In the literature it has also been called MTP-131 and Bendavia, and PubChem lists Ocuvia among its synonyms. The FDA-approved medicine that contains it is Forzinity. The letters SS stand for Szeto-Schiller, after Hazel H. Szeto and P. W. Schiller, the scientists behind the peptide series.
facts: Synthetic tetrapeptide with alternating aromatic and positively charged amino acids; described in its FDA label as a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder

pages.subject: aod-9604
pages.summary: AOD-9604 is a lab-made peptide of 16 amino acids copied from the tail of human growth hormone (residues 177 to 191) plus one extra tyrosine. An Australian company developed it as an obesity drug, but its largest trial found no significant weight loss versus placebo. It is not FDA-approved, and WADA bans it in sport.
faq: Can AOD9604 be taken orally?

Oral use is how it was mostly tested in people: four of the developer's six trials gave it by mouth as capsules or tablets, and two gave it by vein. Animal studies suggest some of an oral dose is absorbed, but FDA says the extent of oral bioavailability is unclear even in animals, and no human study has measured how the body absorbs or clears it. The oral trials also failed to show significant weight loss versus placebo in the largest study.
What is the difference between tirzepatide and AOD-9604?

Tirzepatide is an FDA-approved drug that acts on GIP and GLP-1 receptors, and FDA lists it, as Zepbound, among approved treatments for weight management in obesity. AOD-9604 is an unapproved fragment of human growth hormone whose largest trial found weight loss beyond placebo of under 1 kg, which was not significant. No trial comparing the two was found: ClinicalTrials.gov returned no AOD9604 studies at all when searched in October 2026.
facts: Synthetic fragment of human growth hormone: 16 amino acids (hGH 177 to 191 plus an N-terminal tyrosine)

pages.subject: kisspeptin
pages.summary: Kisspeptin-10 is a 10-amino-acid peptide, the fully active end piece of the hormone kisspeptin-54. It activates the kisspeptin receptor (KISS1R); animal studies show it acts on the brain's GnRH nerve cells, and in people it raises LH. It is not FDA approved, and human studies have been small, using single doses or infusions of up to 22.5 hours.
faq: Is kisspeptin a hormone?

Yes. Kisspeptin is a secreted peptide made from the KISS1 gene, and it works through its own receptor, KISS1R. The NCBI gene record says it regulates the pubertal activation of GnRH nerve cells. WADA lists it with the peptide hormones in section S2 of its Prohibited List, noting that it acts to stimulate GnRH secretion and, as a result, testosterone.
Is kisspeptin FDA approved?

No. As of October 2026, a DailyMed search for kisspeptin returns no drug labels, so there is no approved product and no US prescribing label. FDA keeps Kisspeptin-10 in Category 2 of bulk substances nominated for compounding, the group that raises significant safety risks, on its list updated May 14, 2026. Massachusetts General Hospital studies gave it under FDA oversight, one under an investigational new drug number.
facts: Peptide hormone fragment that activates the kisspeptin receptor (KISS1R, also called GPR54)

pages.subject: igf-1
pages.summary: IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor 1) is a 70-amino-acid hormone that manages the effects of growth hormone. IGF-1 LR3 is a lab-made 83-amino-acid analog studied in cells and rats; ClinicalTrials.gov lists no human trial of it. Recombinant human IGF-1 (mecasermin, Increlex) is a prescription drug for growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency.
faq: What is a normal IGF-1 level by age?

There is no single normal number. IGF-1 is low in childhood, rises to a peak during puberty and falls through adulthood, so a result is read against reference ranges for age and sex.
