NAD+ is not an FDA-approved drug, so there is no approved method, and the diluent volume is a lab choice. The math is the amount in the vial divided by the diluent volume. One registered study dissolved 100 mg of NAD+ in 2 mL of bacteriostatic water, which gives 50 mg per mL. By the same arithmetic, 1,000 mg in 10 mL gives 100 mg per mL, and in 20 mL, 50 mg per mL. Confirm the total amount on the vial label first.

pages.subject: kpv
pages.summary: No human dose of KPV has been established. FDA's 2026 review found no clinical studies and no human pharmacokinetic data for KPV by any route. Published amounts come from mouse experiments, such as KPV at 100 micromolar in drinking water for 8 days, and from cell studies that report concentrations rather than doses.
faq: Can you take KPV every day?

No daily dose, schedule or length of use has been established for KPV in people. FDA found no human studies of KPV and no repeat-dose toxicity studies even in animals, so the safety of daily or long-term use is unknown. One mouse colitis experiment put KPV in the animals' drinking water for 8 days; that describes an experiment, not guidance for people.

pages.subject: zepbound
pages.summary: FDA has approved Zepbound for weight reduction and long-term weight maintenance in adults with obesity, or overweight with a related condition. It is also approved for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. In its largest 72-week trial, average weight loss was 15.0% to 20.9% by dose, against 3.1% on placebo.
faq: What is the average weight loss on Zepbound?

SURMOUNT-1, the largest trial in the label, ran for 72 weeks in adults without type 2 diabetes. Average weight loss was 15.0% on 5 mg, 19.5% on 10 mg and 20.9% on 15 mg, against 3.1% on placebo. In adults with type 2 diabetes it was 12.8% on 10 mg and 14.7% on 15 mg, against 3.2% on placebo.

pages.subject: igf-1
pages.summary: No human trial of IGF-1 LR3 is registered, so its side effects in people have not been studied; what is known comes from recombinant human IGF-1. In Increlex trials of 71 children, 42% had low blood sugar at least once, and high doses in 7 obese adults with diabetes caused swelling, jaw tenderness and a fast heartbeat.
faq: What are the side effects of IGF-1 LR3?

Nobody knows for LR3 itself: no human trial is registered, and anti-doping scientists note that the effects in people of a tagged LR3 found in a black-market vial have not been described. In a long-term study of recombinant IGF-1 in 76 children, the most common problem was low blood sugar, followed by fat buildup at injection sites and enlarged tonsils or adenoids. In 7 obese adults with type 2 diabetes, high doses caused swelling, jaw tenderness, joint pain, fatigue and a fast heartbeat.

pages.subject: thymosin-alpha-1
pages.summary: No dose of Thymosin Alpha-1 is approved in the US, because FDA has approved no drug that contains it. Published doses come from foreign labels for the brand Zadaxin and from clinical trials under medical care, most often 1.6 mg under the skin. FDA notes that the smallest dose needed for a response is hard to determine.
faq: How often can I take thymosin alpha 1?

No schedule can be given for any person, and no US dose exists because no Ta1 drug is FDA approved. For reference only, the Indonesian Zadaxin label used 1.6 mg twice weekly for six months in chronic hepatitis B, and hospital sepsis trials gave 1.6 mg once or twice daily for up to 7 days. FDA notes that the smallest dose needed for a response is hard to determine.

pages.subject: cjc-1295-ipamorelin
pages.summary: Published sources report hormone changes, not proven health benefits, for the two parts of this blend. CJC-1295 with DAC raised growth hormone and IGF-1 for days in small trials, and IV ipamorelin caused a short growth hormone pulse. No study of the blend, or of CJC-1295 without DAC, has measured any outcome in people.
faq: Will CJC-1295 and ipamorelin help build muscle or burn fat?

That has not been shown in people. The human studies measured hormone levels or gut recovery after surgery, not muscle or fat. In mice, ipamorelin increased fat pad weight. A 2026 primer credits the blend with a muscle-force result in steroid-treated rodents, but the study that matches it gave rats ipamorelin alone. Reviews from 2020 and 2026 describe clinical benefit data for these secretagogues as lacking or limited.

pages.h1: CJC-1295 with DAC benefits and uses
pages.subject: cjc-1295-with-dac
pages.summary: Reported benefits of CJC-1295 with DAC are hormone changes: in small studies of healthy adults, one injection raised growth hormone and IGF-1 for about one to two weeks. No study has measured muscle, fat loss, healing, sleep or skin outcomes in people. The only patient trial was terminated, and its data have not been published.
faq: What are the benefits of CJC-1295 with DAC?

The documented effects are hormonal. In placebo-controlled trials of healthy adults, one injection raised GH and IGF-I for about one to two weeks, with an estimated half-life of 5.8 to 8.1 days. No study measured muscle, fat, recovery, sleep or skin outcomes in people, and FDA says the human studies do not support effectiveness for treating growth hormone deficiency. The one patient trial, in HIV-associated abdominal fat, was terminated, and its data have not been published.

pages.subject: aod-9604
pages.summary: In the developer's oral and IV trials, side effects of AOD-9604 were similar to placebo; headache was the most common, and gut symptoms and colds were also frequent. FDA identified no human data for injection under the skin, found too little information to support long-term safety, and has open concerns about immune reactions and the tumors reported in one trial.
faq: Is AOD-9604 safe?

Safety is only partly known. In developer-funded oral and IV trials lasting up to 24 weeks, side effects were similar to placebo, mostly headache, gut symptoms and colds. But FDA concluded in 2024 that safety information is limited: it identified no human data for injection under the skin, found too little information to support long-term safety, warned that injected routes may carry a particular risk of immune reactions, and noted unresolved bone, liver and genotoxicity signals in animal studies.

pages.subject: nad
pages.summary: No human dose of NAD+ injection is established or approved in the US. Small studies gave 750 mg by IV over 6 hours once, or 500 mg by IV daily for 4 days. Another gave 100 mg daily for 3 days under the skin, into muscle or by IV push. These figures describe research, not guidance for people.
faq: Can NAD be given IV?

It has been, in small studies. A 2019 pilot gave 750 mg over 6 hours to 8 healthy men with no adverse events. A 2026 clinic review covered 500 mg a day for 4 days in 6 clients, all of whom reported moderate to severe symptoms during the drip. No IV dose is FDA-approved, because NAD+ is not an approved drug. Pharmacy-compounded NAD+ for a patient needs a valid patient-specific prescription.

pages.subject: glow-peptide
pages.summary: Glow peptide side effects have not been studied, because no published study has tested the blend. Reports come from its ingredients: an FDA case of skin and gum darkening, small human studies with no serious adverse events, and clotting and liver signals in animals. Regulators also warn of immune reactions to injected peptides.
faq: Can the copper in Glow cause problems?

It might, though no study has measured it. Glow's copper comes from GHK-Cu, its main ingredient by weight. A 2026 review says repeated injection should be evaluated for copper build-up in the liver and, at high exposures, the nervous system. The same review found no validated human safety threshold for GHK-Cu. MedlinePlus notes that large amounts of copper are poisonous, and that Wilson disease, a rare inherited disorder, causes copper deposits in the liver and brain.

pages.subject: kpv
pages.summary: KPV benefits reported so far come from cell and animal studies, the largest group of them in mice with chemically induced colitis. FDA's 2026 review found no study of KPV in people and concluded there is a lack of evidence to evaluate it for wound healing or inflammatory conditions. A ClinicalTrials.gov search in October 2026 found no registered KPV trial.
faq: Does KPV peptide really work?

Whether it works in people is unknown, because no human study has tested it: FDA's 2026 review found no clinical studies, case reports or human exposure data for KPV by any route. The positive results come from animals: mice with induced colitis recovered sooner and regained more weight, and rats with chemotherapy mouth sores ate and healed better with a gel carrying KPV and the plant compound EGCG.

pages.subject: thymosin-alpha-1
pages.summary: Thymosin Alpha-1 is approved abroad as the brand Zadaxin, mainly for chronic hepatitis B and as a vaccine adjuvant, but in 2024 FDA found a lack of evidence of effectiveness for all 12 uses it reviewed. Some trials in hepatitis B and sepsis reported benefits that later double-blind, placebo-controlled trials did not confirm.
faq: What is thymosin alpha 1 used for?

Outside the US, the brand Zadaxin is approved mainly for chronic hepatitis B and to boost the flu vaccine response of people with weak immune systems, for example in India and Italy. Researchers have also tested Ta1 in hepatitis C, HIV, cancers, sepsis and COVID-19. In 2024, FDA found a lack of evidence of effectiveness for all 12 uses it reviewed, and no Ta1 product is approved in the US.

pages.subject: klow-peptide
pages.summary: No study has measured side effects of KLOW, so its safety in people is unknown. Reports exist only for its parts: headache and flatulence after BPC-157 enemas, a few FDA adverse event reports and animal safety signals. FDA calls the human safety risks of TB-500 and KPV unknown.
faq: What are the side effects of KLOW?

None have been measured for the blend, because no study has tested it. For its parts, BPC-157 enema studies most often reported headache and flatulence, and FDA lists single reports of injection-site redness, shortness of breath, and skin and gum darkening in people injecting BPC-157 products, without establishing the cause. Animal studies of BPC-157 showed clotting and liver signals. FDA also warns that injected peptides like these may trigger immune reactions.

pages.subject: sermorelin
pages.summary: Freeze-dried sermorelin is dissolved by adding a measured volume of a sterile diluent such as bacteriostatic water, with aseptic technique and gentle swirling, not shaking. No current label sets the volume, so the volume chosen sets the concentration. This page covers supplies, lab steps, concentration math for a 10 mg vial and storage.
faq: Where was sermorelin injected in studies?

In published human studies, sermorelin was injected under the skin, or given into a vein for testing. The Geref International Study Group trial in children used once-daily injections under the skin at bedtime. The studies reviewed here do not compare injection sites on the body. This page covers lab reconstitution only and gives no injection instructions for a research compound.

pages.subject: kpv
pages.summary: No side effects of KPV have been recorded in people, because FDA found no study that gave it to people. FDA's 2026 review also found no case reports and no animal toxicity studies, and it called the potential safety risks of KPV in humans unknown. The risks it names include immune reactions.
faq: Does KPV make you tired?

There is no information either way: FDA found no study that gave KPV to people, so none has looked for tiredness or any other effect, and it found no case reports. Its adverse event database held no KPV reports through December 3, 2025, but reporting is voluntary and pharmacies that compound under section 503A generally do not report, so the empty record does not show that KPV causes no side effects.

pages.subject: rybelsus
pages.summary: Rybelsus is used in adults with type 2 diabetes for two FDA-approved purposes: blood sugar control alongside diet and exercise, and lowering the risk of major cardiovascular events in those at high risk. Its label trials report lower HbA1c on 7 mg and 14 mg, and fewer major cardiovascular events on 14 mg than on placebo.
faq: What is Rybelsus used for?

Rybelsus has two FDA-approved uses, both in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control, its original use from 2019. Since October 2025, it is also used to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke) in those at high risk. It is not approved for weight loss, and the prescriber decides whether it fits a given patient.

pages.subject: melanotan
pages.summary: No human dose of Melanotan 2 (MT2) is established or approved. The only published trial doses come from three small University of Arizona studies (1996 to 2000) that gave 3 to 10 men each a few weight-based injections, at 0.01 to 0.03 mg/kg. They are research doses, not guidance for anyone.
faq: What dose of Melanotan 2 was used in studies?

Weight-based doses of 0.01 to 0.03 mg/kg. The 1996 pilot study raised the dose step by step over five injections under the skin in 3 healthy men, and the two erectile dysfunction trials gave 0.025 mg/kg per injection to 10 men each. Nausea was common, and severe in 12.9% of subjects at 0.025 mg/kg. These figures describe study conditions, not a dose for any person.

pages.subject: kisspeptin
pages.summary: Kisspeptin-10 has no approved medical use. In small human studies, given once or infused for up to 22.5 hours, it raised LH rapidly and raised testosterone in men during infusions. The better-known fertility and sexual-desire results come from the longer-lasting kisspeptin-54, not kisspeptin-10.
faq: Does kisspeptin raise testosterone levels?

In small studies of men, yes, during infusions. A 22.5-hour IV kisspeptin-10 infusion raised testosterone from 16.6 to 24.0 nmol/L in 4 healthy men. An 11-hour infusion raised it from 8.5 to 11.4 nmol/L in 5 men with type 2 diabetes and low testosterone. Single IV doses gave only small rises, and a 75-minute kisspeptin-54 infusion did not change testosterone.

pages.subject: kisspeptin
pages.summary: Kisspeptin-10 has no reported side effects in its small safety record: three studies of 4 to 13 people each found no kisspeptin-related adverse events. With continuous exposure, kisspeptins and their analogs turned the reproductive hormone axis down in human and animal studies. FDA says it lacks the safety information to judge harm.
faq: What are the side effects of kisspeptin?

In the small kisspeptin-10 studies that reported safety, no kisspeptin-related adverse events occurred, with 4 to 13 people in each. Kisspeptin-54 trials also reported good tolerability. With long-acting analogs, the most common drug-related problems were injection-site redness and pain, and continuous dosing lowered testosterone. FDA says it does not have the safety data to know if kisspeptin-10 would harm people, so long-term risks are unknown.

pages.subject: thymosin-alpha-1
pages.summary: In clinical studies of Thymosin Alpha-1, mostly at 1.6 mg under the skin, the most common side effects were irritation, redness or discomfort at the injection site. The most serious reports came from stem cell transplant recipients: engraftment failure and fatal immune destruction of red blood cells. FDA also warns of possible immune reactions to compounded Ta1.
faq: What are the common side effects of thymosin alpha 1?

The most common in clinical studies were irritation, redness or discomfort at the injection site, and in most studies Ta1 was not linked to significant adverse events. The Indonesian label for the brand Zadaxin, as summarized by FDA, lists rare redness, temporary muscle wasting, joint pain with hand swelling, and rash. In an early cancer study, 1 of 14 people had fever and 2 had mild nausea after single doses into the muscle.

pages.subject: ss-31
pages.summary: The only SS-31 (elamipretide) benefit FDA has accepted is improved muscle strength in Barth syndrome, for patients of at least 30 kg, under a 2025 accelerated approval that still awaits confirmation. Larger trials in mitochondrial myopathy, heart failure, heart attack and dry macular degeneration missed their main goals. Most anti-aging data come from mice.
faq: What is SS-31 peptide good for?

Its only approved use is improving muscle strength in Barth syndrome, a rare genetic mitochondrial disease, in patients of at least 30 kg. Researchers have also tested it in mitochondrial myopathy, heart failure, heart attack and dry macular degeneration. In those conditions, the larger trials did not meet their primary goals. The anti-aging case rests mostly on studies in old mice.

pages.subject: dsip-peptide
pages.summary: The human safety record for DSIP is small: FDA counted 209 people given it intravenously in published studies, each for 1 to 15 days. Reported effects include headache, warmth, sweating, nausea, vertigo and, in 2 drug-withdrawal patients, low blood pressure at the first injection. FDA found no safety data for injection under the skin.
faq: How safe is DSIP peptide?

Its safety is not established. The human studies FDA reviewed all gave DSIP intravenously, none for more than 15 days, and FDA describes safety for long-term, on-and-off use as insufficiently characterized. The effects reported range from headache and warmth to low blood pressure in withdrawal patients. FDA also found no safety data for injection under the skin, and it warns that compounded emideltide may trigger immune reactions.

pages.subject: ss-31
pages.summary: Injection site reactions are the most common reported side effect of SS-31 (elamipretide). In the Barth syndrome trial, all 12 patients had one on elamipretide, against 8 of 12 on placebo. The label also warns of serious allergic reactions, and carcinogenicity studies had not been done at approval.
faq: Is SS-31 peptide safe?

No source establishes the safety of research-grade SS-31; the safety data come from clinical trials of elamipretide and the label of the approved product. In a 218-adult phase 3 trial it was well tolerated, with most adverse events mild to moderate. Injection site reactions were very common, serious allergic reactions have occurred, and eosinophil counts often rose for a time. FDA required cancer studies only after approval.

pages.subject: tirzepatide
pages.summary: Approved tirzepatide needs no mixing: Mounjaro and Zepbound come as a ready-to-use solution in pens and vials. The research vial holds a freeze-dried solid with no FDA-reviewed mixing or storage directions, and bacteriostatic water is sold separately. This page covers label use and storage, then lab handling and math for a dry vial.
faq: Where in the thigh to inject tirzepatide?

For the prescribed medicines, the labels list the thigh, the abdomen, or the back of the upper arm when someone else gives the injection, and say to rotate the site with each dose. Drug exposure was similar at all three sites. For a more exact spot on the thigh, the product's Instructions for Use and the prescriber are the sources to follow. None of this applies to research-labeled vials.

pages.subject: dsip-peptide
pages.summary: No benefit of DSIP is established in people. Most reported benefits come from small intravenous studies published from 1981 to 1998, mainly on sleep. One research group reported faster sleep onset and longer sleep, while placebo-controlled trials by two other groups found little benefit. FDA called the sleep evidence inconclusive and at best preliminary.
faq: How much does DSIP help?

It depends on the study design. In the most favorable study, 14 adults with chronic insomnia went from 58.4 to 27.6 minutes to fall asleep over 7 nights, and total sleep rose from 313 to 385 minutes, but that study had no placebo arm. In a randomized, placebo-controlled crossover study of 6 adults with insomnia, the changes were small and, per FDA, not significant against baseline or placebo. No dose for people is established.

pages.subject: aod-9604
pages.summary: Reconstituting AOD-9604 means dissolving the freeze-dried solid in a measured volume of liquid so the vial holds a known concentration. No USP monograph or approved label sets an official method for AOD-9604. A supplier certificate that FDA cites puts the free base's solubility in water at up to 2 mg per mL.
faq: What do you mix AOD-9604 with?

No official diluent is set: AOD-9604 has no USP monograph and belongs to no approved product. In the developer's two IV trials, the freeze-dried drug was mixed with sterile water for injection before use. This vial comes without diluent, and bacteriostatic water is sold separately. Bacteriostatic water contains benzyl alcohol as a preservative.

pages.subject: tb-500
pages.summary: TB-500 is reconstituted by adding a measured volume of diluent to its powder vial, and that volume sets the concentration. Vendor data cited by FDA report that the free base dissolves in water at 50 mg per mL. This page covers supplies, lab steps, concentration math for a 5 mg vial, storage before and after mixing, and the routes used in studies.
faq: Where is TB-500 injected in studies?

Rats received TB-500 by injection into the abdominal cavity, and horses by a single injection under the skin. In an uncontrolled case series, 3 patients received it by injections under the lining of the mouth. FDA found no human data for TB-500 by any route. No injection site has been tested in a controlled study or shown to be safe in people.

pages.subject: pinealon
pages.summary: Side effects of Pinealon in people are largely unknown, because no clinical trial of it is registered. The human record is a few small Russian studies. One, of 32 adults given Pinealon and Vesugen, reported pro-oxidant activity and lower markers of blood-forming stem cells; another rated the peptides among the safest methods tested.
faq: Is Pinealon safe?

No one can say yet: Pinealon has never been tested in a registered clinical trial, so its side effects, how often they occur and its long-term safety are unknown. One small Russian study of Pinealon and Vesugen found pro-oxidant activity and lower markers of blood-forming stem cells. Health Canada says the injectable Pinealon products it seized had not been assessed for safety, efficacy or quality.

pages.h1: How to reconstitute CJC-1295 with DAC
pages.subject: cjc-1295-with-dac
pages.summary: Reconstituting CJC-1295 with DAC means dissolving its freeze-dried powder in a measured volume of liquid for lab use. No official method exists, because no form of CJC-1295 is part of an approved drug or has a USP monograph. FDA, citing a supplier source, reports a water solubility of about 2 mg per mL.
faq: How much bacteriostatic water is used for a 2 mg vial of CJC-1295 with DAC?

No official volume exists, because CJC-1295 has no approved label or USP monograph. The volume simply sets the concentration: 1 mL gives 2 mg per mL, 2 mL gives 1 mg per mL and 3 mL gives about 0.67 mg per mL. FDA reports a water solubility of about 2 mg per mL from a supplier source, so 1 mL is the smallest volume that stays within that figure. The reconstitution calculator works out any other volume.

pages.subject: glp-1
pages.summary: In large placebo-controlled trials lasting 68 to 72 weeks, adults lost an average of 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide 2.4 mg and up to 20.9% on tirzepatide, against 2.4% and 3.1% on placebo. Much of the lost weight returned after treatment stopped. This page reports what trials and labels show, and it makes no promise.
faq: How much weight do people lose on GLP-1 medicines?

Results vary widely between people. In STEP 1, 86.4% of adults on semaglutide 2.4 mg lost at least 5% of body weight. At least 10% was lost by 69.1%, and at least 15% by 50.5%. On placebo the figures were 31.5%, 12.0% and 4.9%. In SURMOUNT-1, 30.0% to 56.7% of adults on tirzepatide lost 20% or more, against 3.1% on placebo.

pages.subject: ozempic
pages.summary: Ozempic is FDA approved, with diet and exercise, to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. In its label trials, HbA1c fell about 1.2 to 2.1 points from starting levels near 8% to 9%, depending on dose and other medicines. This page maps what sources report on Ozempic for type 2 diabetes and makes no promise for any one person.
faq: What does Ozempic actually do for diabetes?

It lowers blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes: semaglutide raises insulin release and lowers glucagon release when blood sugar is high, and it slows stomach emptying. In the label's 30-week trial of Ozempic alone, HbA1c fell 1.4 points on 0.5 mg and 1.6 on 1 mg from a start near 8.1%, against 0.1 on placebo. In adults with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease, outcome trials also found fewer major cardiovascular events and fewer serious kidney and heart events.

pages.subject: semaglutide
pages.summary: In STEP 1, a 68-week trial of 1,961 adults, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg lowered body weight by 14.9% on average, against 2.4% on placebo, with lifestyle intervention in both groups. Wegovy is the semaglutide product FDA approved for weight management, and about two-thirds of the lost weight returned within a year of stopping in follow-up.
faq: Is semaglutide better than tirzepatide?

For weight, the head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial favored tirzepatide. It followed 751 adults with obesity and without type 2 diabetes for 72 weeks. At each drug's maximum tolerated dose, average weight change was -20.2% with tirzepatide vs -13.7% with semaglutide. Waist size fell 18.4 cm vs 13.0 cm, and gastrointestinal effects were the most common side effects with both drugs.

pages.subject: tirzepatide
pages.summary: Tirzepatide is the active ingredient in Zepbound, which FDA approved in November 2023 for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition. In a 72-week trial of 2,539 adults, average weight fell 15.0% to 20.9% versus 3.1% on placebo. Stopping treatment led to substantial weight regain.
faq: How long does it take to lose 20 lbs on tirzepatide?

The trials do not answer that directly. They report average percent changes at fixed time points, and results vary by person. In SURMOUNT-1, doses were raised over 20 weeks, and average weight at 72 weeks was 15.0% to 20.9% lower, versus 3.1% on placebo. How many pounds that means depends on starting weight. We found no sourced figure for pounds lost per month.

pages.subject: ozempic
pages.summary: Ozempic is not approved for weight loss; its label covers adults with type 2 diabetes. Weight still fell in its diabetes trials, by an average of 3.2 to 6.4 kg (about 7 to 14 lb) over 30 to 56 weeks. The semaglutide brand FDA approved for weight reduction is Wegovy, at higher doses. This page reports what sources found on Ozempic for weight loss and makes no promise.
faq: How long will it take to lose 20 lbs on Ozempic?

The label gives no weight-loss timeline, since weight loss is not an approved use. In its diabetes trials, average weight loss on Ozempic ranged from 3.2 to 6.4 kg (about 7 to 14 lb) over 30 to 56 weeks, so no trial average reached 20 lb. In the 30-week trial of Ozempic alone it was 3.8 kg on 0.5 mg and 4.7 kg on 1 mg, and every course starts with 4 weeks at a 0.25 mg starting dose. In STEP 2, adults with type 2 diabetes on 1.0 mg lost 7.2% of body weight on average over 68 weeks.

pages.subject: mounjaro
pages.summary: Weight loss is not a US use of Mounjaro: its FDA label covers blood sugar control and heart risk in type 2 diabetes. Weight was still tracked in its diabetes trials, and average losses ran from about 5.4 to 11.3 kg after 40 to 52 weeks. The same molecule carries a US weight reduction approval under a different brand, Zepbound.
faq: Can Mounjaro be used for weight loss only?

Not under its US label. FDA approved Mounjaro to improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes and to lower the risk of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes; weight loss on its own is not one of those uses. Weight fell in the diabetes trials, but as a measured outcome rather than an approved purpose. In the US, tirzepatide for weight reduction is approved under the Zepbound name. The European Union differs: there, Mounjaro's authorization also covers weight management in adults, alongside diet and physical activity.

pages.subject: wegovy
pages.summary: Wegovy is FDA-approved for long-term weight reduction, always with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity. The approval covers adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, and (injection only) children 12 and older with obesity. In the label's main weight trials of adults without diabetes, average weight change ranged from -13.6% on the tablets to -18.8% on the 7.2 mg injection.
faq: How long does it take to lose 20 lbs with Wegovy?

Trials report percent of body weight over months, not the time to reach a set number of pounds, and results vary by person. In STEP 4, the 803 adults who completed a 20-week run-in, which included the dose climb, had lost 10.6% of body weight on average. In STEP 1, adults on 2.4 mg had lost 14.9% on average by week 68. How many pounds a percentage means depends on starting weight, and the prescriber sets the pace of each dose step.

pages.subject: mounjaro
pages.summary: Improving blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise, is Mounjaro's main US use, for adults and for children 10 and older. Across the label's five adult trials, HbA1c dropped by about 1.7 to 2.4 points after 40 to 52 weeks on 5 to 15 mg once weekly. The prescriber sets and adjusts the dose under the label schedule.
faq: Does Mounjaro ever not work?

Trial results show it does not bring everyone to target. SURPASS-1 tested Mounjaro as the sole diabetes medicine: after 40 weeks, 78% to 85% of adults taking it got below an HbA1c of 7%, so 15% to 22% did not reach that mark, against 23% reaching it on placebo. Some people also stop: 3.0% to 6.6% of adults on 5 to 15 mg stopped treatment because of stomach and gut side effects, against 0.4% on placebo. When more control is needed, the label lets the prescriber raise the dose in 2.5 mg steps, up to 15 mg in adults.

pages.subject: rybelsus
pages.summary: Rybelsus for type 2 diabetes is an FDA-approved daily tablet that, with diet and exercise, improves blood sugar control in adults. In its trial without other diabetes drugs, 77% of adults on 14 mg reached an HbA1c under 7% at 26 weeks, against 31% on placebo. This page maps what sources report; it makes no promise for any person.
faq: Does Rybelsus help with blood sugar?

Yes. Improving blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise, is the use FDA first approved in 2019. The label says semaglutide raises insulin and lowers glucagon when blood sugar is high. In a trial of 731 adults already on insulin, adding Rybelsus 14 mg lowered HbA1c by 1.3 points at week 26, against 0.1 on placebo. The 3 mg starting dose does not count toward this: the label calls it not effective for blood sugar control.

pages.subject: rybelsus
pages.summary: Rybelsus is not FDA approved for weight loss; its label covers adults with type 2 diabetes. Its diabetes trials, whose main measure was HbA1c, also reported weight: at week 26, the largest average change in any group was -4.4 kg on 14 mg. The semaglutide tablet FDA approved for weight reduction is Wegovy.
faq: Does Rybelsus work for weight loss?

Rybelsus is not approved for weight loss; its label covers adults with type 2 diabetes. Weight did fall in its diabetes trials. In the trial against liraglutide injection, 14 mg averaged -4.4 kg at 26 weeks, against -3.1 kg on liraglutide and -0.5 kg on placebo. For weight reduction itself, FDA approved a different semaglutide tablet, Wegovy, in December 2025.

pages.subject: wegovy
pages.summary: Wegovy is not FDA-approved to treat type 2 diabetes or to control blood sugar; its approved uses are weight reduction, heart risk reduction and MASH. In a 68-week trial of 807 adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c fell 1.6 points on Wegovy against 0.4 on placebo. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea.
faq: Is there a diabetic version of Wegovy?

Not under the Wegovy name. The semaglutide brands approved for type 2 diabetes are Ozempic, a weekly injection, and Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets, taken daily. Ozempic's weekly doses top out at 2 mg, while Wegovy's maintenance dose is 2.4 mg and can reach 7.2 mg for adult weight reduction. Wegovy itself is approved for weight, heart risk and MASH, not for blood sugar control.

pages.subject: pt-141
pages.summary: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is not FDA approved for men: the Vyleesi label says it is not indicated for HSDD in men or to enhance sexual performance. Studies in men are small trials from 2004 and 2005, mostly of a nasal form, plus a 2008 trial of 342 men that now carries an expression of concern.
faq: What happens if a male takes PT-141?

In studies published in 2004, injected doses above 1 mg in healthy men, and nasal doses above 7 mg compared with placebo, produced statistically significant erectile responses. Flushing and nausea were the most common side effects in the nasal studies. With the approved injection, each dose briefly raised blood pressure and slowed heart rate, usually back to baseline within 12 hours. Bremelanotide is not FDA approved for men, and no dose for men has been established.

pages.subject: semaglutide
pages.summary: Semaglutide for diabetes is FDA approved as Ozempic injection and as Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets, to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. In a 30-week Ozempic trial, HbA1c fell 1.4 to 1.6 points vs 0.1 on placebo. These are group averages, and whether it suits a patient is a prescriber's decision.
faq: What happens if you take semaglutide without diabetes?

Wegovy's weight and heart indications do not require diabetes, and the SELECT trial enrolled 17,604 adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity but no history of diabetes. The Wegovy label lists low blood sugar as a common side effect only in patients with type 2 diabetes; digestive side effects are the most common for everyone. Use without diabetes is still prescription only and set by a prescriber.

pages.subject: tirzepatide
pages.summary: Tirzepatide is approved as Mounjaro to improve blood sugar control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. In 40-week trials, HbA1c dropped by roughly 1.9 to 2.3 percentage points, more than with semaglutide 1 mg. Over 3 years in adults with obesity and prediabetes, 1.3% were diagnosed with type 2 diabetes versus 13.3% on placebo.
faq: Is tirzepatide approved for type 2 diabetes?

Yes. FDA approved it as Mounjaro on May 13, 2022. The current label covers blood sugar control, with diet and exercise, in adults and children 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes, and lowering cardiovascular risk in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. It is a prescription medicine. In the EU, Mounjaro was authorised in September 2022.

pages.subject: sermorelin
pages.summary: No published trial reviewed here shows sermorelin causes weight or fat loss. In the one sermorelin study that measured body fat, 6 weeks of nightly injections in 11 older men changed neither weight nor DEXA fat. In a test of 23 women, obesity blunted the growth hormone response to the same peptide. This page maps that evidence and makes no promise.
faq: Does sermorelin help with fat loss?

No published trial in the sources reviewed here shows it. In 11 older men, 6 weeks of nightly injections did not change weight, BMI, waist-to-hip ratio or DEXA fat. In a test of 14 obese and 9 normal-weight women, obesity blunted the GH response to GRF(1-29). Tesamorelin, an FDA-approved GHRH analog, is labeled not for weight loss management because it has a weight neutral effect.

pages.subject: pt-141
pages.summary: Bremelanotide (PT-141) is FDA approved, as Vyleesi, only for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD). In two 24-week trials of 1,267 such women it improved desire and desire-related distress more than placebo, by small average margins, and 40% had nausea. It is not approved after menopause.
faq: How well does PT-141 work for women?

In two 24-week trials of 1,267 premenopausal women with HSDD, bremelanotide raised desire scores 0.30 to 0.42 points more than placebo and lowered distress about low desire 0.29 to 0.37 points more. It did not increase the number of satisfying sexual events. Independent re-analyses in 2021 and 2024 judged the benefits small or statistically modest, and the trial investigators disputed the 2021 re-analysis.

pages.subject: sermorelin
pages.summary: No study reviewed here shows sermorelin building muscle mass. In 11 men aged 64 to 76, six weeks of nightly injections improved 2 of 6 strength measures, but DEXA muscle mass did not change. The evidence comes from small, short studies in older adults, and a 2026 review judges benefits in healthy people uncertain.
faq: Does sermorelin build muscle?

Not on the evidence so far. Eleven men aged 64 to 76 given nightly injections for 6 weeks did better on 2 of 6 strength tests and one endurance test, while DEXA muscle mass and muscle tissue under the microscope did not change. Only a related analog, not sermorelin, added lean mass, and only in the 9 men, over 16 weeks. A 2026 review finds clinically meaningful benefits in healthy people uncertain.

pages.summary: Tirzepatide is the active ingredient; Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's once-weekly tirzepatide injection for type 2 diabetes, and the same molecule is labeled in the US as Zepbound for weight reduction and sleep apnea.
faq: Is tirzepatide the same as Mounjaro?

Mounjaro contains tirzepatide, but the two words name different things. Tirzepatide is the active ingredient. Mounjaro is one FDA-approved product made with it, labeled for adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. Zepbound is Lilly's other tirzepatide brand, labeled for weight reduction and sleep apnea. FDA has warned companies that sold unapproved tirzepatide falsely labeled 'for research purposes' to consumers, and says unapproved versions do not undergo its review for safety, effectiveness and quality.

pages.summary: GLP-1 is a gut hormone and the name of the drug class that mimics it, while Mounjaro is one brand-name drug in that group whose active ingredient, tirzepatide, activates the GLP-1 receptor and a second hormone receptor, the GIP receptor.
faq: Is Mounjaro a GLP-1 medication?

Yes, with a second target. FDA's 2024 list of approved GLP-1 receptor agonists includes Mounjaro, and notes that tirzepatide is a dual GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist. Its label calls tirzepatide a GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist, so it activates two hormone receptors. Semaglutide, by contrast, selectively binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor. So Mounjaro is grouped with the GLP-1 drugs, but it is not a GLP-1-only drug.

pages.summary: GLP-1 is a natural gut hormone and the name of a drug class, while semaglutide is one drug in that class: a modified copy of the hormone that shares 94% of its sequence, activates the same receptor and has an elimination half-life of about one week.
faq: Is semaglutide a GLP-1 inhibitor?

No. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist, which means it switches the receptor on rather than blocking it. It selectively binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor, the same target the body's own hormone uses. Through that receptor it raises insulin release and lowers glucagon, both in a glucose-dependent way, and causes a minor delay in stomach emptying soon after meals.

pages.summary: Semaglutide is the active ingredient and Wegovy is one brand of it: Novo Nordisk's semaglutide for long-term weight reduction, cardiovascular risk reduction and a liver disease, given at higher doses than the diabetes brands Ozempic and Rybelsus.
faq: What is the generic name for Wegovy?

Semaglutide. Wegovy injection and Wegovy tablets both contain it, and it is the same active ingredient found in Ozempic and Rybelsus. All of these are Novo Nordisk products, but each brand has its own label, doses and approved uses. Wegovy is the one approved for long-term weight reduction, for lowering the risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight, and for MASH, a liver disease.

pages.summary: Mounjaro and Ozempic are both once-weekly type 2 diabetes injections, but they contain different molecules from different makers: Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's tirzepatide, which acts on GIP and GLP-1 receptors, and Ozempic is Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, which selectively acts on GLP-1 receptors.
faq: Is Mounjaro the same as Ozempic?

No. They contain different active ingredients from different makers. Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's tirzepatide, which acts on GIP and GLP-1 receptors; Ozempic is Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, which acts on GLP-1 receptors only. Both are once-weekly injections for adults with type 2 diabetes, and both labels include a cardiovascular use. Ozempic also has a kidney indication and a tablet form, while Mounjaro's diabetes use extends to children 10 and older.

pages.summary: Semaglutide is the active ingredient and Ozempic is one finished product made with it: Novo Nordisk's type 2 diabetes medicine, a weekly injection and, since a January 2026 FDA approval, also a daily tablet.
faq: Is Ozempic the same as semaglutide?

Not exactly. Semaglutide is the drug substance, a GLP-1 analog and receptor agonist. Ozempic is a finished Novo Nordisk medicine built around it, with its own formulation, pens, doses and label for adults with type 2 diabetes. The same substance is in Rybelsus tablets, at different doses, and in Wegovy, which has different doses and approved uses. So every Ozempic dose is semaglutide, but semaglutide is not always Ozempic.

pages.summary: Ozempic and Wegovy contain the same drug, semaglutide, from the same maker, but Ozempic is labeled for adults with type 2 diabetes while Wegovy is labeled for weight reduction, for cardiovascular risk in adults with cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight, and for a liver disease.
faq: Is Wegovy the same as Ozempic?

They share an active ingredient, semaglutide, and a maker, Novo Nordisk, but they are separate products with separate FDA labels. Ozempic is approved for adults with type 2 diabetes. Wegovy is approved for long-term weight reduction, for lowering cardiovascular event risk in adults with cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight, and for the liver disease MASH. Wegovy's usual maintenance dose, 2.4 mg a week, is also above Ozempic's 2 mg maximum.

pages.summary: Ozempic is a brand of semaglutide, which acts on the GLP-1 receptor, while tirzepatide is a different molecule, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, that acts on both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors.
faq: Is tirzepatide the same as Ozempic?

No. Ozempic contains semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk. Tirzepatide is a different molecule from Eli Lilly that acts on two receptors, GIP and GLP-1, and is sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound. The two also sit on different dose scales: Ozempic runs from 0.25 to 2 mg weekly and Mounjaro from 2.5 to 15 mg weekly, so milligrams cannot be swapped between them.

pages.summary: Mounjaro and Wegovy differ in molecule, maker and approved job: Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's tirzepatide for type 2 diabetes, and Wegovy is Novo Nordisk's semaglutide for weight reduction, heart risk and a liver disease.
faq: Which is better, Wegovy or Mounjaro?

It depends on what is being treated, because their labels differ. Mounjaro is approved for type 2 diabetes and for heart risk in type 2 diabetes; Wegovy for weight reduction, for heart risk in adults with cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight, and for a fatty liver disease, MASH. For weight, the head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial, in 751 adults with obesity but without type 2 diabetes, measured average losses of 20.2% with tirzepatide against 13.7% with semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg across 72 weeks.

pages.summary: Rybelsus is one product, a once-daily semaglutide tablet for adults with type 2 diabetes, while semaglutide is the molecule inside it and inside the Ozempic and Wegovy injections and tablets.
faq: Can you get semaglutide in a tablet?

Yes. As of October 2026, three FDA-approved products are semaglutide tablets taken once a day. Rybelsus (3, 7 and 14 mg) and Ozempic tablets (1.5, 4 and 9 mg) are for adults with type 2 diabetes. Wegovy tablets (1.5, 4, 9 and 25 mg) are for weight reduction and heart risk in adults. All three are prescription medicines, and each has its own starting dose and steps.

pages.summary: Ozempic and Rybelsus both contain semaglutide from Novo Nordisk; the main difference is the route, a once-weekly injection for Ozempic and a once-daily tablet for Rybelsus, though the Ozempic name now also covers a tablet.
faq: What are the key differences between Ozempic and Rybelsus?

Both contain semaglutide from Novo Nordisk and are approved for adults with type 2 diabetes. Ozempic is mainly a weekly injection of 0.25 to 2 mg and also carries a kidney indication; Rybelsus is a daily tablet of 3 to 14 mg taken on an empty stomach. Storage differs too: Ozempic pens are refrigerated before first use, while Rybelsus is kept at room temperature.

pages.summary: Mounjaro is Eli Lilly's brand of tirzepatide, which activates both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, while semaglutide, the active ingredient in Novo Nordisk's Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus, activates the GLP-1 receptor only.
faq: Is semaglutide better than tirzepatide?

In both head-to-head trials, tirzepatide produced larger average changes. In SURPASS-2, HbA1c fell 2.0 to 2.3 points on tirzepatide against 1.9 on semaglutide 1 mg over 40 weeks. In SURMOUNT-5, in adults with obesity but without type 2 diabetes, weight fell 20.2% against 13.7% over 72 weeks. Neither trial settles which drug suits a given person. That depends on the condition being treated, other medicines and side effects, and it is a prescriber's decision.

pages.summary: A peptide amount is written as a mass, in milligrams (mg) or micrograms (mcg), or in units, and the amount in a syringe depends on two numbers: the volume drawn and the concentration of the solution. On a U-100 syringe, each unit mark is 0.01 mL of liquid, not an amount of drug. Approved prescription medicines are dosed by the prescriber, following the label. Research vials carry no human dose: an unapproved drug shipped for lab research must be labeled "Not for use in humans".
faq: How do you read the units on an insulin syringe?

Each unit line on a U-100 insulin syringe stands for 0.01 mL, so the full 1 mL barrel reads 100 units, 10 units is 0.1 mL and 50 units is 0.5 mL. On the same scale, 0.5 mL and 0.3 mL barrels hold up to 50 and 30 units; embecta, one maker, sells both sizes and says U-500 insulin always takes a U-500 syringe. The units measure volume only, so the amount of drug they hold depends on the concentration of the liquid.

pages.summary: Peptide safety rests on four checks: a batch certificate with numerical results, sterile handling, correct storage and knowing the side effects sources report. Laboratory tests of peptide products bought online have found wrong amounts, impurities and bacterial endotoxin, and FDA warns that injected products get past some of the body's natural defenses against toxins and microbes.
faq: What are the side effects of peptides for weight loss?

For approved GLP-1 medicines, the labels list them, and the GLP-1 side effects page collects them. Compounded and research-labeled versions are not FDA approved, so FDA does not review them for safety, effectiveness or quality before sale. By May 31, 2026, FDA had received 990 adverse event reports tied to compounded semaglutide and more than 730 tied to compounded tirzepatide. Adverse events reported after overdoses from measuring mistakes with compounded semaglutide included nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fainting, dehydration, acute pancreatitis and gallstones.

pages.summary: A subcutaneous injection places medicine in the fatty tissue just under the skin, not in muscle. This guide describes how prescribed subcutaneous injections are given, following patient guides from the US National Library of Medicine, the American Diabetes Association, the NHS and FDA: sites, rotation, clean technique and sharps disposal. It is not a guide to injecting any research compound.
faq: Where do you give a subcutaneous injection?

MedlinePlus names three areas: the belly, at least 2 inches from the belly button; the outer upper thighs; and the side or back of the upper arms, at least 3 inches below the shoulder and above the elbow. NHS medicine pages for weekly semaglutide and tirzepatide name the thigh, tummy and upper arm. The skin should be healthy, and injections are spaced at least an inch apart. The instructions supplied with a prescribed product take priority.

pages.h1: How to reconstitute a peptide vial
pages.summary: Reconstitution dissolves a freeze-dried (lyophilized) peptide in a measured volume of sterile diluent, so the vial holds a known concentration. Labels for approved freeze-dried medicines show the technique: let the diluent run down the vial's inner wall, swirl or roll it gently, never shake it, and use the solution only if it is clear. This guide covers lab handling only.
faq: How many mL of bacteriostatic water do you mix with a peptide?

There is no universal volume. The bacteriostatic water label hands that decision to the manufacturer of the drug being dissolved, who weighs its concentration, dose and route. Approved products print their own figure: 1.3 mL for the 11.6 mg EGRIFTA WR vial and 1.14 mL for the 5.8 mg Omnitrope vial. A research peptide has no label, so the volume follows from the concentration the work needs: volume equals the amount in the vial divided by the target concentration. The reconstitution calculator shows that arithmetic.

pages.summary: Freeze-dried peptides keep best cold, dry, dark and tightly closed: peptide makers advise a freezer for long-term storage, and Bachem accepts a refrigerator at 4 °C for short-term use. Peptides in solution have a much shorter shelf life, so makers advise against storing them that way, and approved products set their own limits once mixed, from immediate use to 60 days.
faq: Should peptides be stored in the fridge or the freezer?

For freeze-dried powder, peptide makers favor the freezer for long-term storage: below -15 °C according to Bachem, or -20 °C away from bright light according to GenScript. Bachem accepts a 4 °C refrigerator for short-term use. Approved freeze-dried medicines differ by label, from room temperature for tesamorelin to 2 to 8 °C for ZOMACTON somatropin, so a vial's own label comes first. Dissolved peptides follow separate, stricter rules.

faq: How much bacteriostatic water should be added to a peptide vial?

No single volume is correct. The bacteriostatic water label leaves the volume to the maker of the drug being mixed, based on that drug's concentration, dose and route. Labeled products state their own, such as 1.3 mL per EGRIFTA WR vial. To reach a set concentration, divide the amount in the vial by that concentration.

pages.summary: This converter changes mg to mcg and mL to U-100 syringe units, in either direction, and turns IU into mg only with a factor stated for that exact product. A syringe unit is a volume, a milligram is a weight and an IU measures biological activity, so the converter keeps them apart. FDA said confusion between mL, mg and units may have contributed to dosing errors reported to it.
faq: How many units are in 1 mL on an insulin syringe?

On a U-100 syringe, 100. U-100 means 100 units in each mL; it is the most common insulin strength, and most insulin syringes are marked for it. Each unit is therefore 0.01 mL. Stronger insulin, such as U-500, has its own syringe: embecta, a syringe maker, says to always use a U-500 syringe for U-500 insulin. Check which scale a syringe is made for before converting a reading.

faq: What does an HPLC purity figure on a certificate mean?

HPLC (high-performance liquid chromatography) is a liquid chromatography technique that uses high inlet pressure and offers high sensitivity and speed. A purity figure describes how free the sample is of impurities, and EMA lists purity, as total and individual impurities, among the tests in a peptide's specification. Identity is a separate test, often run by mass spectrometry, whose variants can measure a peptide's molecular mass and confirm its sequence of amino acids. So read the method next to every number, and look for an identity result as well as a purity figure.
Does a 99% purity figure mean the vial holds the labeled amount?

No. Purity and quantity are separate results. Purity describes how free the material is of impurities, while quantity is how much peptide the vial actually holds. A 2024 laboratory study of semaglutide vials bought online measured drug content with liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry and reported it apart from purity: content ran above the label while purity measured far below the labels' claim. A certificate that gives only a purity figure leaves the amount in the vial unmeasured, so look for both.

faq_groups.title: What a compound is
items: What is BPC-157?

A lab-made peptide of 15 amino acids, described as part of a protein found in human gastric juice. Evidence comes mostly from animal studies: a 2026 systematic review found only three human studies, with 30 people in all and no control groups. No country has approved a medicine containing it.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/peptides/bpc157/
Is tirzepatide a peptide?

Yes. It is a 39-amino-acid peptide joined to a fatty-acid chain, and it activates two gut-hormone receptors, GIP and GLP-1. It is the active ingredient in Mounjaro, approved for type 2 diabetes, and Zepbound, approved for long-term weight reduction and for sleep apnea in adults with obesity.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/peptides/tirzepatide/

faq_groups.title: Research goals
items: Do peptides help with healing?

The evidence differs by compound and is mostly from animals. A 2025 systematic review of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine found 36 studies, of which 35 were preclinical and 1 was clinical. Animal results do not show what happens in people, so each compound's profile reports its evidence level.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/goals/healing/
Do growth hormone peptides build muscle?

This has not been shown. Human studies of CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 measured growth hormone and IGF-1 levels, appetite, diagnosis or gut recovery, not muscle growth. Even growth hormone itself raised lean mass by 2.1 kg in a review of healthy young adults without improving strength or exercise capacity.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/goals/muscle/

faq_groups.title: Side effects and safety
items: What are the side effects of GLP-1 drugs?

Stomach and gut effects are the most common: on the Ozempic label, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and constipation each affected 5% or more of patients. The label also warns of pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea, and thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/glp-1/side-effects/
Do GLP-1 drugs cause suicidal thoughts?

FDA's review found no increased risk. A meta-analysis of 91 placebo-controlled trials with 107,910 patients showed no rise in suicidal thoughts or behavior, and in January 2026 FDA asked makers to remove that warning from the Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels. FDA still advises anyone with new or worsening depression to tell a health care professional.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/glp-1/side-effects/

items: Do you give dosing advice?

Research-grade vials are unapproved and have no label dose. How much tirzepatide do the labels start with?

Both tirzepatide labels start at 2.5 mg once weekly. If more blood sugar control is needed, Mounjaro rises in 2.5 mg steps after at least 4 weeks on each dose, to a maximum of 15 mg weekly for adults. Zepbound treats 2.5 mg as a starting dose only, moves to 5 mg after 4 weeks, and lists maintenance doses of 5, 10 or 15 mg for weight reduction. The prescriber sets the dose.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/peptides/tirzepatide/dosage/

faq_groups.title: Reconstitution and calculation
items: How do I work out the concentration after mixing?

Divide the amount in the vial by the volume of diluent added. A 10 mg vial mixed with 2 mL holds 5 mg/mL, so each 0.1 mL holds 0.5 mg, and 0.1 mL is 10 units on a U-100 syringe. The reconstitution calculator and units converter do the same math and show the formula.

How many mL of bacteriostatic water go into a vial?

There is no single volume. The volume chosen sets the concentration, so less liquid gives a stronger solution and more gives a weaker one, and the calculator shows the result for any volume. Approved products fix their own: EGRIFTA WR is mixed with 1.3 mL of bacteriostatic water to give 8 mg per mL.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/guides/how-to-reconstitute/

faq_groups.title: Comparisons
items: Is Ozempic the same as semaglutide?

Ozempic is one FDA-approved brand of semaglutide for adults with type 2 diabetes: a weekly injection, also approved to lower heart and kidney risks in some of them, and now a daily tablet too. Wegovy is semaglutide approved for long-term weight reduction, and Rybelsus is a daily semaglutide tablet for type 2 diabetes.
/d2cpeptides-redesign/learn/compare/ozempic-vs-semaglutide/
Is Zepbound the same as Mounjaro?

Both contain tirzepatide and are made by Eli Lilly, but they are approved for different uses. Mounjaro is for type 2 diabetes: blood sugar control in adults and children 10 and older and, since August 2026, cutting the risk of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults. Zepbound is for long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, and for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.
